gh issue create --title "Plugin-health pass: mark Plugin-owned Skills and offer Plugin Next" --label "enhancement,ready-for-agent" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
# Plugin-health pass

Grill settled 2026-08-23 (Plugin-health). Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` § Plugin-health pass. Parent direction: Runner-first this pass; later product idea B (binary for Runner) is **not** this spec.

Seams (existing): `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot`; Review result + Scan `HealthEntry`; spawn CLI (`runDoraval`) for review / scan / fix text and JSON.

`dora review <plugin-root>` already walks owned Skills. `dora fix <plugin-root>` already can apply mechanical fixes there. This spec does not add a new verb or a new fix engine.

## Problem Statement

A Runner that hits a Plugin-owned Skill cannot tell it is inside a Plugin. `dora skill unused` / `remove` skip those Skills (v0.6.23). Next after a named remove is `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`. Review and Scan still look like any other Skill. After `dora fix` of that Skill, nothing offers the rest of the Plugin. The user wants health read/report that names the Plugin and offers a dry-run update of the Plugin, without making Plugin and Skill the same unit.

## Solution

Plugin and Skill stay separate units. `dora review` of a Plugin-owned Skill path is allowed (that Skill only) and says Plugin-owned. `dora review <plugin-root>` stays today’s Review and lists owned Skills. `dora fix` of that Skill still writes that Skill. On Review of that Skill, on its Scan health row, and after that `fix`: print Plugin-owned; Next is `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` and `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`. JSON on those three surfaces adds `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot`. No top-level `next` array. No Plugin-wide `--yes`. No new `dora plugin` verb. No Subagent Review. `unused` / `remove` / `restore` still skip Plugin-owned Skills.

## User Stories

1. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick <plugin-owned-skill>` to succeed, so that I can grade one Skill inside a Plugin.
2. As a Runner, I want that Review to say the Skill is Plugin-owned, so that I do not treat it as a standalone Authored Skill.
3. As a Runner, I want that Review’s Next to include `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`, so that I can grade the rest of the Plugin.
4. As a Runner, I want that Review’s Next to include `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`, so that I have an option to update the Plugin without `--yes`.
5. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick --json` on that Skill to include `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot`, so that I can branch without parsing the table.
6. As a Runner, I want a standalone Skill’s Review JSON to omit those fields (or set `pluginOwned: false` with no `pluginRoot`), so that I do not invent a Plugin.
7. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` to review owned Skills the same way as today, so that I do not learn a new report format.
8. As a Runner, I want each owned Skill in that Plugin-root Review to also carry `pluginOwned` / `pluginRoot` in JSON, so that the unit is still visible.
9. As a Runner, I want `dora scan --json` health rows for Plugin-owned Skills to include `pluginOwned` and `pluginRoot`, so that the map matches Review.
10. As a Runner, I want Scan’s human table to mark those rows Plugin-owned, so that a human on a TTY sees the same fact.
11. As a Runner, I want Scan Next (or the row) to offer the two Plugin commands when any Plugin-owned Skill is present, so that I am not sent to `dora skill remove`.
12. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-owned-skill> --yes` to still apply mechanical fixes to that Skill only, so that Mechanical improve does not change.
13. As a Runner, I want after that `fix` (table mode) the same Plugin-owned mark and two Next lines, so that I can opt into the Plugin.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-owned-skill> --json` to include `pluginOwned` and `pluginRoot` on the result, so that I can opt in from JSON.
15. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run` to keep today’s behavior (preview mechanical fixes under that tree), so that the Next command is not a lie.
16. As a detected agent, I want Plugin-wide write to still need `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that we never auto `--yes` the whole Plugin.
17. As a Runner, I want no new `dora plugin` command, so that I keep using review and fix.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora skill unused` to still omit Plugin-owned Skills, so that v0.6.23 does not regress.
19. As a Runner, I want named `dora skill remove` of a Plugin-owned Skill to still exit `1` with Next to `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`, so that writes stay last pass’s rule.
20. As a Runner, I want Imported and Global rules unchanged, so that Plugin-owned stays a separate predicate.
21. As a Runner, I want Finding messages to still say Remove candidate, not “unused”, so that R034 language stays clean.
22. As a Reader on a TTY, I want Review/Scan/fix tables to still render, so that we do not drop human output this pass.
23. As a Runner, I want no new TTY picker for Plugin vs Skill, so that this pass stays Runner-first.
24. As a Runner, I want `pluginRoot` to be the ancestor that holds the Plugin manifest, stopped at cwd, so that it matches v0.6.23 detection.
25. As a Runner, I want lockstep docs only if a printed line would otherwise lie (Review/Scan/fix Next, skill if it still says unused is the only Plugin story), so that we do not rewrite the site.
26. As a founder, I want Subagent Review out of this spec, so that this pass is Plugin health only.
27. As a founder, I want later idea B (binary only for Runner) out of this spec, so that we do not delete tables or old confirms now.
28. As an implementer, I want one spawn-CLI seam for the three surfaces, so that tests match what agents see.
29. As an implementer, I want to reuse `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot`, so that unused/remove and health agree.
30. As a Runner using `--ci`, I want JSON plus the two fields, so that CI can branch.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Units.** Plugin and Skill stay separate. Do not refuse Skill-path Review or Skill-path fix.
- **Plugin Review.** `dora review <plugin-root>` is today’s `review(path)` over `findSkillDirs`. No new report envelope.
- **Mark.** Human: say Plugin-owned (short). JSON: `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot` (absolute path of the manifest ancestor). Standalone Skills: no `pluginRoot`; `pluginOwned` false or omitted.
- **Where.** (1) Review of a Plugin-owned Skill (and each such Skill inside a Plugin-root Review). (2) Scan `HealthEntry` for those Skills. (3) After `dora fix` of that Skill (table Next; JSON fields on the fix payload).
- **Next (table).** Two lines, in this order: `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` then `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`. Keep existing Next (e.g. skill-path `dora fix`) if still true. Do not add a top-level JSON `next` array.
- **Fix.** Skill-path fix unchanged. Plugin-root `--dry-run` / `--yes` unchanged (write gate stays). Do not invent Plugin-wide apply-without-flag.
- **Detection.** Reuse `isPluginOwned(dir, cwd)` and `pluginRoot(dir, cwd)`. Stop at cwd. Manifest = `plugin.json` or provider marketplace file (already in classify).
- **Do not change** `listRemoveCandidates`, named remove/restore refuse, unused skip.
- **Runner-first.** No new TTY picker. Table may stay. No human-only chrome.
- **Docs.** Lockstep only if a line would lie. No new pages. No version bump in this spec.
- **Modules.** Review result shape + review CLI render/Next; Scan health shape + Scan render/Next; fix CLI after-skill Next + JSON fields. Classify already exists.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior: argv in, stdout/stderr/JSON/exit out.
- **Seam 1:** `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot` — already tested; add only if health wiring needs a new case.
- **Seam 2 (primary):** spawn CLI. Fixture: project with one standalone Skill and one Plugin (manifest + owned Skill).
  - `review --quick --json` on the owned Skill → `pluginOwned` true, `pluginRoot` is the Plugin dir.
  - `review --quick --json` on the standalone Skill → not Plugin-owned.
  - `review --quick` (table) on the owned Skill → “Plugin-owned” and both Next commands.
  - `scan --json` → health row for the owned Skill has the two fields.
  - `fix --dry-run --json` on the owned Skill → payload includes the two fields; files unchanged.
- **Seam 3:** Scan/Review unit if cheaper than spawn for health-entry shape (`HealthEntry` / `ReviewResult`).
- Prior art: `test/cli.test.ts` (review/scan/fix JSON), `src/core/scan.test.ts`, `src/core/skill-classify.test.ts` (Plugin-owned), issue #45 spawn + classify.
- Do not add a live marketplace install test. Do not add Subagent fixtures.

## Out of Scope

- New `dora plugin` verb
- Subagent Review
- Plugin-wide `--yes` without the existing write gate
- Top-level JSON `next` array
- Changing unused / remove / restore
- MCP, hooks, research-notes extras
- Dropping tables or TTY confirms (later idea B)
- Version bump / npm release

## Further Notes

- Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` § Plugin-health pass. v0.6.23 Agent-contract pass stays.
- Next: `/to-tickets`. Suggest: (1) stamp `pluginOwned`/`pluginRoot` on Review + Scan JSON and human mark, (2) Plugin Next on Review + Scan + after fix. (1) can start immediately; (2) blocked by (1) only if Next needs the same stamp.

EOF
)"

gh issue create --title "Plugin-health pass: mark Plugin-owned Skills and offer Plugin Next" --label "enhancement,ready-for-agent" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
# Plugin-health pass

Grill settled 2026-08-23 (Plugin-health). Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` § Plugin-health pass. Parent direction: Runner-first this pass; later product idea B (binary for Runner) is **not** this spec.

Seams (existing): `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot`; Review result + Scan `HealthEntry`; spawn CLI (`runDoraval`) for review / scan / fix text and JSON.

`dora review <plugin-root>` already walks owned Skills. `dora fix <plugin-root>` already can apply mechanical fixes there. This spec does not add a new verb or a new fix engine.

## Problem Statement

A Runner that hits a Plugin-owned Skill cannot tell it is inside a Plugin. `dora skill unused` / `remove` skip those Skills (v0.6.23). Next after a named remove is `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`. Review and Scan still look like any other Skill. After `dora fix` of that Skill, nothing offers the rest of the Plugin. The user wants health read/report that names the Plugin and offers a dry-run update of the Plugin, without making Plugin and Skill the same unit.

## Solution

Plugin and Skill stay separate units. `dora review` of a Plugin-owned Skill path is allowed (that Skill only) and says Plugin-owned. `dora review <plugin-root>` stays today’s Review and lists owned Skills. `dora fix` of that Skill still writes that Skill. On Review of that Skill, on its Scan health row, and after that `fix`: print Plugin-owned; Next is `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` and `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`. JSON on those three surfaces adds `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot`. No top-level `next` array. No Plugin-wide `--yes`. No new `dora plugin` verb. No Subagent Review. `unused` / `remove` / `restore` still skip Plugin-owned Skills.

## User Stories

1. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick <plugin-owned-skill>` to succeed, so that I can grade one Skill inside a Plugin.
2. As a Runner, I want that Review to say the Skill is Plugin-owned, so that I do not treat it as a standalone Authored Skill.
3. As a Runner, I want that Review’s Next to include `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`, so that I can grade the rest of the Plugin.
4. As a Runner, I want that Review’s Next to include `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`, so that I have an option to update the Plugin without `--yes`.
5. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick --json` on that Skill to include `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot`, so that I can branch without parsing the table.
6. As a Runner, I want a standalone Skill’s Review JSON to omit those fields (or set `pluginOwned: false` with no `pluginRoot`), so that I do not invent a Plugin.
7. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` to review owned Skills the same way as today, so that I do not learn a new report format.
8. As a Runner, I want each owned Skill in that Plugin-root Review to also carry `pluginOwned` / `pluginRoot` in JSON, so that the unit is still visible.
9. As a Runner, I want `dora scan --json` health rows for Plugin-owned Skills to include `pluginOwned` and `pluginRoot`, so that the map matches Review.
10. As a Runner, I want Scan’s human table to mark those rows Plugin-owned, so that a human on a TTY sees the same fact.
11. As a Runner, I want Scan Next (or the row) to offer the two Plugin commands when any Plugin-owned Skill is present, so that I am not sent to `dora skill remove`.
12. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-owned-skill> --yes` to still apply mechanical fixes to that Skill only, so that Mechanical improve does not change.
13. As a Runner, I want after that `fix` (table mode) the same Plugin-owned mark and two Next lines, so that I can opt into the Plugin.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-owned-skill> --json` to include `pluginOwned` and `pluginRoot` on the result, so that I can opt in from JSON.
15. As a Runner, I want `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run` to keep today’s behavior (preview mechanical fixes under that tree), so that the Next command is not a lie.
16. As a detected agent, I want Plugin-wide write to still need `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that we never auto `--yes` the whole Plugin.
17. As a Runner, I want no new `dora plugin` command, so that I keep using review and fix.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora skill unused` to still omit Plugin-owned Skills, so that v0.6.23 does not regress.
19. As a Runner, I want named `dora skill remove` of a Plugin-owned Skill to still exit `1` with Next to `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`, so that writes stay last pass’s rule.
20. As a Runner, I want Imported and Global rules unchanged, so that Plugin-owned stays a separate predicate.
21. As a Runner, I want Finding messages to still say Remove candidate, not “unused”, so that R034 language stays clean.
22. As a Reader on a TTY, I want Review/Scan/fix tables to still render, so that we do not drop human output this pass.
23. As a Runner, I want no new TTY picker for Plugin vs Skill, so that this pass stays Runner-first.
24. As a Runner, I want `pluginRoot` to be the ancestor that holds the Plugin manifest, stopped at cwd, so that it matches v0.6.23 detection.
25. As a Runner, I want lockstep docs only if a printed line would otherwise lie (Review/Scan/fix Next, skill if it still says unused is the only Plugin story), so that we do not rewrite the site.
26. As a founder, I want Subagent Review out of this spec, so that this pass is Plugin health only.
27. As a founder, I want later idea B (binary only for Runner) out of this spec, so that we do not delete tables or old confirms now.
28. As an implementer, I want one spawn-CLI seam for the three surfaces, so that tests match what agents see.
29. As an implementer, I want to reuse `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot`, so that unused/remove and health agree.
30. As a Runner using `--ci`, I want JSON plus the two fields, so that CI can branch.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Units.** Plugin and Skill stay separate. Do not refuse Skill-path Review or Skill-path fix.
- **Plugin Review.** `dora review <plugin-root>` is today’s `review(path)` over `findSkillDirs`. No new report envelope.
- **Mark.** Human: say Plugin-owned (short). JSON: `pluginOwned: true` and `pluginRoot` (absolute path of the manifest ancestor). Standalone Skills: no `pluginRoot`; `pluginOwned` false or omitted.
- **Where.** (1) Review of a Plugin-owned Skill (and each such Skill inside a Plugin-root Review). (2) Scan `HealthEntry` for those Skills. (3) After `dora fix` of that Skill (table Next; JSON fields on the fix payload).
- **Next (table).** Two lines, in this order: `dora review --quick <plugin-root>` then `dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`. Keep existing Next (e.g. skill-path `dora fix`) if still true. Do not add a top-level JSON `next` array.
- **Fix.** Skill-path fix unchanged. Plugin-root `--dry-run` / `--yes` unchanged (write gate stays). Do not invent Plugin-wide apply-without-flag.
- **Detection.** Reuse `isPluginOwned(dir, cwd)` and `pluginRoot(dir, cwd)`. Stop at cwd. Manifest = `plugin.json` or provider marketplace file (already in classify).
- **Do not change** `listRemoveCandidates`, named remove/restore refuse, unused skip.
- **Runner-first.** No new TTY picker. Table may stay. No human-only chrome.
- **Docs.** Lockstep only if a line would lie. No new pages. No version bump in this spec.
- **Modules.** Review result shape + review CLI render/Next; Scan health shape + Scan render/Next; fix CLI after-skill Next + JSON fields. Classify already exists.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior: argv in, stdout/stderr/JSON/exit out.
- **Seam 1:** `isPluginOwned` / `pluginRoot` — already tested; add only if health wiring needs a new case.
- **Seam 2 (primary):** spawn CLI. Fixture: project with one standalone Skill and one Plugin (manifest + owned Skill).
  - `review --quick --json` on the owned Skill → `pluginOwned` true, `pluginRoot` is the Plugin dir.
  - `review --quick --json` on the standalone Skill → not Plugin-owned.
  - `review --quick` (table) on the owned Skill → “Plugin-owned” and both Next commands.
  - `scan --json` → health row for the owned Skill has the two fields.
  - `fix --dry-run --json` on the owned Skill → payload includes the two fields; files unchanged.
- **Seam 3:** Scan/Review unit if cheaper than spawn for health-entry shape (`HealthEntry` / `ReviewResult`).
- Prior art: `test/cli.test.ts` (review/scan/fix JSON), `src/core/scan.test.ts`, `src/core/skill-classify.test.ts` (Plugin-owned), issue #45 spawn + classify.
- Do not add a live marketplace install test. Do not add Subagent fixtures.

## Out of Scope

- New `dora plugin` verb
- Subagent Review
- Plugin-wide `--yes` without the existing write gate
- Top-level JSON `next` array
- Changing unused / remove / restore
- MCP, hooks, research-notes extras
- Dropping tables or TTY confirms (later idea B)
- Version bump / npm release

## Further Notes

- Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` § Plugin-health pass. v0.6.23 Agent-contract pass stays.
- Next: `/to-tickets`. Suggest: (1) stamp `pluginOwned`/`pluginRoot` on Review + Scan JSON and human mark, (2) Plugin Next on Review + Scan + after fix. (1) can start immediately; (2) blocked by (1) only if Next needs the same stamp.

EOF
)"

<skill name="to-tickets">
# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

<local-ticket-template>

# <NN> — <Ticket title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

</local-ticket-template>

<issue-template>

## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

## What to build

The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Blocked by

- A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

</issue-template>

In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

</skill>
</skill_information>

When a Runner reviews a Plugin-owned Skill, sees it on Scan, or finishes `dora fix` of that Skill, Next is:

`dora review --quick <plugin-root>`

`dora fix <plugin-root> --dry-run`

The idea is still fuzzy. You want a new capability. You do not yet have a locked shape.

`agent-traces` is a **Python** tool. It reads JSONL traces. It writes three tables: sessions, events, content. It uses **Polars** and **Parquet**. Those are analysis stores. Polars is a table library. Parquet is a compact file format.

Doraval already parses sessions in **Bun / TypeScript**. That work lives in `src/core/session-adapters/` and `SessionPrimitives`. `dora sessions` lists them. Review and unused already use them as evidence.

So the job is **not** “port the Python repo.” The job is “decide what analysis Doraval still lacks.”

1. **`/research`** — a background agent reads the GitHub repo and our session code. It writes one cited note in the repo. It does not write product code.
2. **`/grill-with-docs`** — we lock one product question from that note.

Do **not** run `/implement` now. Do **not** add Python, Polars, or Parquet.

Doraval uses a Session as **evidence** (did this skill run?).

`agent-traces` uses a Session as a **research corpus** (errors, cost, tool mix, health).

Those are different jobs. The grill must pick one.

1→# Research notes (session capture)

Scratch we reuse for the developer journey and product ideas. **Split by topic** so files stay readable.

Companion journey doc: [`developer-journey.md`](./developer-journey.md).

Deleted local-only clutter (authorized): `docs/specs/`, `docs/superpowers/`, root `plans/`.

## Index
10→
- [`01-agent-core-and-tools.md`](./research-notes/01-agent-core-and-tools.md) — Claude agentic loop: models vs tools, Claude tools (by category)…
- [`02-sessions-and-context.md`](./research-notes/02-sessions-and-context.md) — Claude Code: where transcripts & auto memory live, Claude Code: three runtime environments…
- [`03-memory-and-rules.md`](./research-notes/03-memory-and-rules.md) — How Claude remembers your project (full page note)
- [`04-skills.md`](./research-notes/04-skills.md) — Extend Claude with skills (full reference + invocation/skillOverrides product notes)
- [`05-subagents-and-teams.md`](./research-notes/05-subagents-and-teams.md) — Create custom subagents (full page note), Agent teams (orchestrate multiple Claude Code sessions)
- [`06-mcp.md`](./research-notes/06-mcp.md) — Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP (full reference + quickstart)
- [`07-hooks.md`](./research-notes/07-hooks.md) — Hooks guide + full reference (matchers, I/O, async, decision schemas)
- [`08-artifacts.md`](./research-notes/08-artifacts.md) — Share session output as artifacts
- [`09-compare-combine-costs.md`](./research-notes/09-compare-combine-costs.md) — Compare similar features (decision matrix), Combine features & context costs
20→- [`10-claude-directory.md`](./research-notes/10-claude-directory.md) — Explore the `.claude` directory (layout map)
- [`11-doraval-product-ideas.md`](./research-notes/11-doraval-product-ideas.md) — Build your setup over time (progressive context maturity), Journey idea: dora suggests context improvements from sessions…
- [`12-plugins-and-marketplaces.md`](./research-notes/12-plugins-and-marketplaces.md) — Discover/install + create + plugins reference (schema, CLI, versioning)
- [`13-channels.md`](./research-notes/13-channels.md) — Channels user guide + build reference (webhook, reply, permission relay)
- [`14-scheduled-tasks.md`](./research-notes/14-scheduled-tasks.md) — Run prompts on a schedule (`/loop`, cron tools, vs Routines/Desktop)

**Status:** research only. Do not edit Doraval CLI from this file.

You are doing /research for the Doraval repo at /Users/saif/Experiments/doraval.

## Question

What is https://github.com/davanstrien/agent-traces actually (architecture, schema, formats, analyses), and how does it map onto Doraval's existing session stack? The product intent: make session analysis a fundamental Doraval capability, in the current Bun/TypeScript stack — not a Python/Polars port.

This is research only. Do not change Doraval product code. Do not add deps. Do not implement.

## Primary sources only

Follow every claim back to the file that owns it. No blogs unless the repo itself points at them as first-party.

### A. agent-traces (clone, do not assume README is enough)

Clone shallow to /tmp/agent-traces-research:
```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/davanstrien/agent-traces.git /tmp/agent-traces-research
```
Record HEAD commit SHA.

Read at least:
- README.md, agent.md, pyproject.toml
- All Python under agent_traces/ (parsers, schema, dataset, CLI, tables)
- tests/ (what they lock)
- Any ATIF / format detection code

Document:
1. Purpose in one sentence from the source.
2. Supported formats and how detection works (file + function).
3. The three-table layout: exact column names for sessions / events / content. Cite the schema source file.
4. Flat 44-column table: what it is and whether it is legacy.
5. Parse pipeline: JSONL → Entry → tables. Cite types.
6. Aggregates: tool_counts, token_stats, error_rate, summary, cost — what they compute, from which columns.
7. CLI surface (convert, inspect, flags).
8. Hub ingest vs local files.
9. Session-health / predictor claims: only if the repo actually implements them; if the README mentions AUC 0.84 but code does not contain a predictor, say so.
10. License, deps (polars, msgspec, etc.), Python version.
11. What it does NOT do (no skill-unused, no review of SKILL.md, no write-back to agent context).

### B. Doraval session stack (this repo)

Read:
- CONTEXT.md glossary rows for Session, Review window, Never invoked, Remove candidate
- src/core/session-parse.ts (SessionPrimitives, ToolCall)
- src/core/session-adapters/types.ts + each adapter (claude, grok, cursor, codex, copilot)
- src/core/sessions-view.ts, session-evidence.ts, session-eval.ts
- src/cli/commands/sessions.ts and sessions/show.ts
- How review / unused / skill-classify use sessions (grep detectUsageInSession, listSessions, SESSION_WINDOW)

Document:
1. What SessionPrimitives already captures vs agent-traces sessions/events/content.
2. Which agents Doraval parses vs agent-traces (overlap + unique each side).
3. What analyses Doraval already runs (invoke evidence, review window last 10 / 30 days, unused).
4. Gaps: tokens, cost, is_error, per-event table, parquet export, Hub corpora, Pi, ATIF.
5. Existing seams: SessionAdapter.parse, SessionPrimitives — would a deeper analysis layer sit on top of these, or would it replace them?

### C. Mapping (the point of the note)

A comparison table:
- Format coverage
- Grain (one Session blob vs 3 tables)
- Analyses
- Storage
- Product job (evidence for context quality vs research corpus)

Then 4–8 grill questions the human must answer later. Do not answer them. Examples of the kind of question (rewrite from sources, don't invent product):
- Extend SessionPrimitives or add a new event table?
- Keep Review window (10/30d) or allow full-corpus analysis?
- Stay on local agent logs only, or also ingest Hub/ATIF?
- Analysis as new `dora` verb vs deepen review/sessions?

YAGNI note: do not recommend porting Polars/Parquet/Python. State what Bun already has that could compute the same aggregates if we wanted them.

`/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval/docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md`

- STE100-ish: short sentences, tables for comparisons, no fluff

Do NOT edit docs/research-notes.md (parent will add the index row).

1→# 48 agent-traces vs Doraval sessions

**Captured:** 2026-08-24
**Status:** research only. Do not edit Doraval CLI from this file.
**Product intent:** make session analysis a fundamental Doraval capability, in the current Bun/TypeScript stack. Not a Python/Polars port.

---

## Primary sources
10→
**agent-traces clone:** `/tmp/agent-traces-research`
**HEAD:** `63df6415bdd651c49d66f161665e000c5c6d94f2` (“Initial release: agent-traces v0.1.0”)
**Remote:** https://github.com/davanstrien/agent-traces

Read: `README.md`, `agent.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, all of `agent_traces/` (`__init__.py`, `parser.py`, `dataset.py`, `schemas.py`, `cli.py`, `hub.py`), `tests/` (`conftest.py`, `test_unit.py`, `test_dataset.py`, `test_integration.py`, `test_bench.py`), fixtures `tests/fixtures/0xkobolds_sample.jsonl` and `tests/fixtures/vtcode_atif_sample.jsonl`.

**Doraval (this repo):**
- `CONTEXT.md` glossary (Session, Review window, Never invoked, Remove candidate)
- `src/core/session-parse.ts` (`SessionPrimitives`, `ToolCall`)
20→- `src/core/session-adapters/types.ts` + `claude.ts` / `grok.ts` / `cursor.ts` / `codex.ts` / `copilot.ts`
- `src/core/sessions-view.ts`, `session-evidence.ts`, `session-eval.ts`
- `src/cli/commands/sessions.ts`, `src/cli/commands/sessions/show.ts`
- Callers: `review.ts`, `scan.ts`, `skill/unused.ts`, `skill-remove.ts`, `artifact-registry.ts`, `memory-file-review.ts`

Did not download Hub corpora. Did not run pytest. Did not edit `src/`.

Cite clone files as `/tmp/agent-traces-research/…:line`. Cite GitHub as `https://github.com/davanstrien/agent-traces/blob/63df6415bdd651c49d66f161665e000c5c6d94f2/…`.

---
30→
## A. agent-traces

### 1. Purpose (one sentence)

Parse multi-format agent session traces into Polars DataFrames and Parquet for analytical workflows: behavioral analysis, cost tracking, error patterns, training data curation.

Source: `/tmp/agent-traces-research/README.md:3–5`. `pyproject.toml:4` is narrower: “Parse pi-share-hf session JSONL files into Polars DataFrames and Parquet.”

### 2. Supported formats and detection
40→
Four formats. Auto-detect is per file.

| Format | `AgentFormat` value | Detection (code, not README) | Parser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pi | `"pi"` | First JSONL line `type` in `session`, `message`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `session_info`, `custom_message`, `compaction`, `label`, `branch_summary`, `custom` | `_parse_pi` |
| Claude Code | `"claude-code"` | First line `type` in `user` / `assistant` / `system`, or `last-prompt` / `queue-operation` / `progress` / `file-history-snapshot` | `_parse_claude` |
| Codex | `"codex"` | First line has a `"payload"` key | `_parse_codex` |
| ATIF | `"atif"` | File-level: first byte `{`, then `json.load` and key `"lines"` | `_parse_atif_file` |

50→Sources:
- Enum: `/tmp/agent-traces-research/agent_traces/parser.py:33–37`
- Line detect: `parser.py:232–268` (`detect_format`)
- ATIF file detect: `parser.py:491–514` (`_is_atif_file`)
- Dispatch: `parser.py:593–651` (`parse_file_multi`)
- Tests lock this: `tests/test_unit.py:151–207`

**README vs code.** README table says ATIF detection is a “First-byte `|` check” (`README.md:103`). Code does not check `|`. ATIF fixture starts with `{\n  "lines": [` (`tests/fixtures/vtcode_atif_sample.jsonl:1–2`). `detect_format` never sees ATIF; `parse_file_multi` peels ATIF off before JSONL.

**README vs code (Claude).** README says detection is `` `type` + `uuid`/`sessionId` `` (`README.md:101`). `detect_format` only inspects `type` (and `payload` for Codex). It does not read `uuid` or `sessionId`.
60→
No Grok. No Cursor. No Copilot. No OpenCode.

### 3. Three-table layout (canonical columns)

Owner is `dataset.py`, not `schemas.py`. `schemas.py` holds the **flat** 44-column map only. Its docstring says the msgspec Structs were dropped; parsing uses `Entry` in `parser.py` (`schemas.py:1–6`). Nothing imports `schemas.py`.

**sessions** — 1 row per session. 15 columns. Source: `dataset.py:22–38` (`SESSIONS_SCHEMA`).

| Column | Type |
70→| --- | --- |
| `session_id` | String |
| `agent` | String |
| `model` | String |
| `provider` | String |
| `version` | Int64 |
| `cwd` | String |
| `start_ts` | String |
| `n_events` | Int64 |
| `n_user_msgs` | Int64 |
80→| `n_assistant_msgs` | Int64 |
| `n_tool_calls` | Int64 |
| `n_errors` | Int64 |
| `input_tokens_total` | Int64 |
| `output_tokens_total` | Int64 |
| `cost_total_sum` | Float64 |

Build: `_build_sessions` (`dataset.py:467–585`). Model coalesce order: session entry → `model_change` → first message with model (`agent.md:49`; `dataset.py:542–554`). Count nulls fill to 0.

**events** — 1 row per entry. 20 columns. Source: `dataset.py:40–61` (`EVENTS_SCHEMA`). Built in `_build_events` (`dataset.py:587–619`). `seq` = ordinal rank of `line_number` within `session_id`. Flat `parentId` aliases to `parent_id`.
90→
| Column | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `session_id` | String |
| `seq` | Int64 |
| `type` | String |
| `agent` | String |
| `role` | String |
| `id` | String |
| `parent_id` | String |
100→| `timestamp` | String |
| `tool_name` | String |
| `stop_reason` | String |
| `is_error` | Boolean |
| `input_tokens` | Int64 |
| `output_tokens` | Int64 |
| `cache_read` | Int64 |
| `cost_total` | Float64 |
| `model` | String |
| `provider` | String |
110→| `thinking_level` | String |
| `exit_code` | Int64 |
| `custom_type` | String |

**content** — 1 row per entry that has text. 9 columns. Source: `dataset.py:63–73` (`CONTENT_SCHEMA`). Filter: any of `content_text`, `content_thinking`, `tool_calls`, `command` is non-null (`dataset.py:631–636`).

| Column | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `session_id` | String |
| `seq` | Int64 |
120→| `content_text` | String |
| `content_thinking` | String |
| `tool_calls` | String |
| `tool_name` | String |
| `tool_call_id` | String |
| `command` | String |
| `output` | String |

Tests lock column sets: `tests/test_dataset.py:31–34` (sessions), `49–50` (events has `seq`), `137–140` (flat == `ALL_COLUMNS`).

130→### 4. Flat 44-column table — yes, legacy

`parser.py:42–88` (`SCHEMA` / `ALL_COLUMNS`) and the unused twin in `schemas.py:10–57`. `Entry.to_row()` (`parser.py:218–226`) owns the contract. `TraceDataset.flat` (`dataset.py:262–266`) and `to_flat_parquet` (`dataset.py:461–463`) exist for backward compat.

`agent.md:17` and `agent.md:41` call it “legacy, kept for backward compat.” README sizes (`README.md:122–127`): for `pi-mono`, flat is 36,791 × 44 vs three tables 626 + 36,791 + 16,841.

Exact 44 names, in schema order: `session_file`, `line_number`, `type`, `agent`, `session_id`, `id`, `parentId`, `timestamp`, `version`, `cwd`, `provider`, `model`, `thinking_level`, `role`, `stop_reason`, `content_text`, `content_thinking`, `tool_calls`, `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, `is_error`, `command`, `output`, `exit_code`, `cancelled`, `truncated`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read`, `cost_total`, `name`, `custom_type`, `display`, `summary`, `first_kept_entry_id`, `tokens_before`, `read_files`, `modified_files`, `from_hook`, `target_id`, `label`, `from_id`, `data`, `raw`.

### 5. Parse pipeline: JSONL → Entry → tables

140→```
JSONL lines → msgspec decode → Entry (dataclass)
                                     │
                         ┌───────────┼───────────┐
                         ▼           ▼           ▼
                    sessions     events      content
```

Source: `README.md:109–118`; `agent.md:29–35`; code `parser.py:600–651` then `dataset.py:91–97` + builders.

150→Types:
- `_decode(line)` → `dict | None` (`parser.py:22–27`). msgspec. Malformed line → skip.
- `detect_format(line)` → `AgentFormat | None` (`parser.py:232–268`).
- Per-format parse → `Entry | None`.
- `Entry` (`parser.py:164–226`): format-agnostic IR. Required: `session_file`, `line_number`, `type`, `agent`. Everything else optional.
- `ContentResult` (`parser.py:103–110`) from `extract_content` (`parser.py:113–158`). Handles str / dict / list of text, thinking, `toolCall`/`tool_use`, `input_text`, image → `"[image]"`.
- `Entry.to_row()` → 44-col dict. `_entries_to_df` (`parser.py:670–676`) → Polars with `SCHEMA`.
- `TraceDataset(entries)` lazily builds the three tables from `self.flat`.

Session id: first line via `_find_session_id` (`parser.py:654–664`), then lazy update if a later entry sets it (`parser.py:649–650`). Pi session entry **is** the session id (`parser.py:299`). Codex: `payload.id` or `payload.session_id` (`parser.py:479`). Claude: `sessionId` on the line (`parser.py:402`). ATIF: `thread.started` → `thread_id` (`parser.py:551–555`).
160→
ATIF is not JSONL. It is one JSON object with a `lines` array (`parser.py:517–588`). Fixture schema_version is `"0.4.0"`.

### 6. Aggregates — what they compute

All live in `TraceDataset` (`dataset.py:395–449`). They are Polars group-bys. No trained model.

| Method | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_counts(group_by="model")` | `tool_calls` view (`tool_name` not null **or** `type` contains `"tool"`) joined to sessions | rows: `group_by`, `tool_name`, `count` |

| **Product job** | Research corpus: Hub datasets, cost, errors, training-data curation. | Evidence for context quality: did this Skill get used, should we remove it, did the agent follow it. |

Exact 44 names, in schema order: `session_file`, `line_number`, `type`, `agent`, `session_id`, `id`, `parentId`, `timestamp`, `version`, `cwd`, `provider`, `model`, `thinking_level`, `role`, `stop_reason`, `content_text`, `content_thinking`, `tool_calls`, `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, `is_error`, `command`, `output`, `exit_code`, `cancelled`, `truncated`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read`, `cost_total`, `name`, `custom_type`, `display`, `summary`, `first_kept_entry_id`, `tokens_before`, `read_files`, `modified_files`, `from_hook`, `target_id`, `label`, `from_id`, `data`, `raw`.

### 5. Parse pipeline: JSONL → Entry → tables

```
JSONL lines → msgspec decode → Entry (dataclass)
                                     │
                         ┌───────────┼───────────┐
                         ▼           ▼           ▼
                    sessions     events      content
```

Source: `README.md:109–118`; `agent.md:29–35`; code `parser.py:600–651` then `dataset.py:91–97` + builders.

Types:
- `_decode(line)` → `dict | None` (`parser.py:22–27`). msgspec. Malformed line → skip.
- `detect_format(line)` → `AgentFormat | None` (`parser.py:232–268`).
- Per-format parse → `Entry | None`.
- `Entry` (`parser.py:164–226`): format-agnostic IR. Required: `session_file`, `line_number`, `type`, `agent`. Everything else optional.
- `ContentResult` (`parser.py:103–110`) from `extract_content` (`parser.py:113–158`). Handles str / dict / list of text, thinking, `toolCall`/`tool_use`, `input_text`, image → `"[image]"`.
- `Entry.to_row()` → 44-col dict. `_entries_to_df` (`parser.py:670–676`) → Polars with `SCHEMA`.
- `TraceDataset(entries)` lazily builds the three tables from `self.flat`.

Session id: first line via `_find_session_id` (`parser.py:654–664`), then lazy update if a later entry sets it (`parser.py:649–650`). Pi session entry **is** the session id (`parser.py:299`). Codex: `payload.id` or `payload.session_id` (`parser.py:479`). Claude: `sessionId` on the line (`parser.py:402`). ATIF: `thread.started` → `thread_id` (`parser.py:551–555`).

ATIF is not JSONL. It is one JSON object with a `lines` array (`parser.py:517–588`). Fixture schema_version is `"0.4.0"`.

### 6. Aggregates — what they compute

All live in `TraceDataset` (`dataset.py:395–449`). They are Polars group-bys. No trained model.

| Method | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_counts(group_by="model")` | `tool_calls` view (`tool_name` not null **or** `type` contains `"tool"`) joined to sessions | rows: `group_by`, `tool_name`, `count` |
| `token_stats(group_by="model")` | `sessions` | `input_tokens` = sum `input_tokens_total`; `output_tokens` = sum `output_tokens_total`; `cost_total` = sum `cost_total_sum`; `n_sessions` = len |
| `error_rate(group_by="model")` | events where `role` contains `"tool"`, joined to sessions | `total`, `errors` = sum `is_error`, `error_rate` = errors/total |
| `session_durations()` | events with non-null `timestamp` | per `session_id`: `duration` (max−min datetime), `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `n_events`. Parse is on demand (`agent.md:110`) |
| `summary()` | all three tables | human string: session/event/content counts, agents, top models, user/assistant/tool/error counts (`dataset.py:667–687`) |

Cost is not a separate method. It is `cost_total_sum` on sessions and the `cost_total` column inside `token_stats`. Pi fills `cost_total` from `message.usage.cost.total` (`parser.py:357–362`). Claude fills tokens, not cost (`parser.py:414–420`). Codex parser does not fill tokens or cost (`parser.py:436–485`). ATIF fills tokens on `turn.completed` / `turn.failed` (`parser.py:559–564`).

`is_error` is filled only on Pi `toolResult` (`parser.py:367`). Claude, Codex, and ATIF parsers do not set it.

Convenience views (not aggregates): `user_messages` (turn / nTurns / normPos + session metadata; `content_text` renamed `msg`), `assistant_messages`, `tool_calls`, `conversation(session_id)`.

### 7. CLI surface

Entry: `agent-traces = agent_traces.cli:main` (`pyproject.toml:16`). Click group (`cli.py:12–15`).

| Command | Flags | What it actually does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `convert SOURCE` | `-o/--output`, `--from-file`, `--output-dir` | Hub id (`/` and path does not exist) → `hub.parse_hub_dataset_to_parquet` (flat parquet). Local glob/dir → `parser.write_parquet` (also flat). `--from-file` = one repo id per line, write `{repo}.parquet` under `--output-dir` (default `parsed/`) |
| `inspect SOURCE` | none | Hub: count JSONL files. Local: count glob matches. **Does not call `summary()`.** |
| `--version` | Click `version_option` | package version |

No `analyze` subcommand. `agent.md:122` lists it as a next step.

CLI writes the **flat** 44-col parquet, not the three-table layout. Three-table export is Python-only: `TraceDataset.to_parquet(dir)` → `sessions.parquet` + `events.parquet` + `content.parquet` (`dataset.py:453–459`).

### 8. Hub ingest vs local files

**Hub**
- `TraceDataset.from_hub(repo_id)` (`dataset.py:102–119`): `list_dataset_files` then `hf_hub_download` each JSONL.
- `hub.list_dataset_files` (`hub.py:14–19`): `list_repo_files`, keep `*.jsonl`, skip `manifest.jsonl`.
- `from_hub_search(tag="format:agent-traces")` (`dataset.py:122–161`): `huggingface_hub.list_datasets(filter=tag)`.
- `from_hub_batch` (`dataset.py:164–217`): explicit repo list, or search. Tags each entry’s `session_file` with the repo id when empty. Impure (`agent.md:106`).
- `hub.parse_hub_dataset` / `parse_hub_dataset_to_parquet`: same download path; output is the flat table.

**Local**
- `TraceDataset.from_dir(path)` (`dataset.py:220–228`): `path/*.jsonl` if directory, else glob.
- `parse_sessions(path_pattern)` (`parser.py:679–691`): glob → list of `Entry` → flat DataFrame. Public export.

Hub example ids in README: `badlogicgames/pi-mono`, `0xSero/pi-sessions`, `moikapy/0xKobolds`, `ultralazr/claude-code-traces`, `cfahlgren1/agent-sessions-list`, `vinhnx90/vtcode-sessions`. Integration tests download one file each of Pi / Claude / Codex from `cfahlgren1/agent-sessions-list` (`tests/conftest.py:32–55`). Locked entry counts (`agent.md:139–145`; `tests/test_integration.py`): Pi 613, Claude 35, Codex 65 on those sample files.

### 9. Session-health / predictor claims

README (`README.md:154–156`): “behavioral features … predict session outcomes with AUC 0.84 after just 2 turns … See the [blog post](#).” The blog link is a dead `#` anchor.

`agent.md:131`: listed under **Research Directions**, not under implemented API. Adds “0.95 overall” and “cheap reward signal in RL training.”

**No predictor exists in this tree.** Grep for `sklearn`, `AUC`, `predictor` hits only those two markdown lines. `scikit-learn>=1.8.0` is in `pyproject.toml:12` and unused. No fit, no features, no AUC test.

### 11. What it does NOT do

- No skill-unused / never-invoked / remove-candidate logic.
- No review of `SKILL.md`.
- No write-back into agent context.
- No adapters that find logs on disk (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, …). Caller passes files or a Hub repo.
- No Grok / Cursor / Copilot / OpenCode parsers.
- No session-health model (see §9).
- No `from_parquet` round-trip (`agent.md:118`).
- No conversation threading on `parentId` (`agent.md:127`).
- CLI `inspect` does not print `summary()`.
- CLI convert does not write the three-table layout.

---

## B. Doraval session stack

### Glossary (product words)

From `CONTEXT.md:28–33`:

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Session** | Past agent conversation transcript, normalized via session adapters into primitives for evidence and adherence eval. |
| **Review window** | Last 10 Sessions, and only Session files newer than 30 days. |
| **Never invoked** | A Skill with no invoke evidence in Sessions inside the Review window. Not a remove candidate. |
| **Remove candidate** | An Authored Skill that is Never invoked and not a Recent install. |

Code constants: `SESSION_WINDOW = 10`, `SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 30`, `SESSION_MAX_FILE_BYTES = 50 * 1024 * 1024` (`src/core/session-adapters/types.ts:19–21`). `withinWindow` (`types.ts:24–26`). Recent install = `withinWindow(skill mtime)` (`src/core/skill-remove.ts:214–216`).

### 1. What `SessionPrimitives` already captures

```8:22:src/core/session-parse.ts
export interface SessionPrimitives {
  sessionId: string;
  sessionTitle?: string;
  model: string;
  agent: string;
  cwd: string;
  gitBranch?: string;
  toolCalls: ToolCall[];
  toolCallCounts: Record<string, number>;
  skillsInvoked: string[];
  userMessages: string[];
  userTurnCount: number;
  durationMs?: number;
  assistantText: string[];
}
```

`ToolCall` (`session-parse.ts:1–6`): `name`, `input`, `timestamp`, `index`.

This is **one blob per session**. Not three tables. Not one row per event.

| agent-traces | Doraval today |
| --- | --- |
| sessions.session_id / agent / model / cwd | `sessionId` / `agent` / `model` / `cwd` |
| sessions.start_ts | file `mtime` on `LoadedSession` / list entry `when`. Not inside primitives. Claude may set `durationMs` from a system line |
| sessions.n_user_msgs / n_assistant_msgs / n_tool_calls / n_errors | `userTurnCount`, `assistantText.length`, `toolCalls.length`. **No `n_errors`.** |
| sessions.input_tokens_total / output_tokens_total / cost_total_sum | **Not on primitives.** Optional `SessionListItem.tokens` (Codex sqlite `tokens_used`; Grok `signals.contextTokensUsed`). `sessions show` prints `Tokens: unavailable` (`show.ts:109`) |
| sessions.provider / version | absent (except Codex `model` is filled from `model_provider`) |
| events.* (seq, type, role, is_error, tokens, parent_id, …) | **No event table.** Tool calls are a list. User/assistant text are string arrays. Sequence is `ToolCall.index` only |
| content.* | `userMessages`, `assistantText`, `ToolCall.input`. No thinking field. Grok keeps only first 5 user messages (`grok.ts:192`) |
| skills / invoke evidence | **`skillsInvoked`** — unique to Doraval. Claude: Skill tool + `attributionSkill` + `<command-name>` + hook text. Grok: ACP titles / `SKILL.md` paths. Cursor/Codex/Copilot leave this `[]` |

`parseSession` in `session-parse.ts` is the **Claude Code** parser. Other agents implement their own parse and still return `SessionPrimitives`.

### 2. Agents: overlap and unique

| Agent | Doraval | agent-traces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | yes — `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/*.jsonl` | yes — same JSONL shape (`type` user/assistant/system) |
| Codex | yes — sqlite `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite` then walk `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` | yes — `payload` wrapper; no sqlite |
| Grok | yes — `~/.grok/sessions/<group>/<id>/updates.jsonl` | no |
| Cursor | yes — `~/.cursor/projects/<dir>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl` | no |
| Copilot | yes — `~/.copilot/session-store.db` + `session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` | no |
| Pi | no | yes |
| ATIF (e.g. vtcode) | no | yes |

Overlap is Claude Code + Codex only. Detection also differs. Doraval: “is the agent home dir on this machine?” (`SessionAdapter.detect`). agent-traces: “what is the first line of this file?”

### 3. Analyses Doraval already runs

All sit on `loadRecentSessions` (`session-evidence.ts:31–56`): each detected adapter, last `SESSION_WINDOW` files, drop mtime older than 30 days, drop files > 50 MB, `adapter.parse`.

| Job | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invoke evidence | Match skill name via `skillsInvoked` (native), tool-input path containing `SKILL.md` / skill dir, or `/name` mention in user text | `session-evidence.ts:64–78` |
| Review tier 4 | `collectSessionEvidence` → sess-001 invoked / sess-002 never invoked / sess-007 remove candidate / sess-003 no sessions | `review.ts:297–323`; `session-evidence.ts:84–143` |
| Scan R034 | Same collect; keep the R034 (remove candidate) finding | `scan.ts:195–212` |
| `dora skill unused` | `listRemoveCandidates` = authored + not plugin-owned + `!skillWasInvoked` + not recent install | `skill/unused.ts`; `skill-remove.ts:227–245` |
| `detectUsageInSession` | `skillsInvoked` exact / `:${name}` / `/${name}` | `artifact-registry.ts:35–38` |
| Memory review | Presence (sess-004) + binding-rule inventory. Optional `runEval` on newest session vs memory file | `memory-file-review.ts:82–124`, `394–419` |
| Adherence eval | LLM judge on truncated tool calls + first 5 user msgs + first 10 assistant texts vs SKILL.md / memory | `session-eval.ts` `buildEvalPrompt` / `runEval` |
| `dora sessions` | Table: agent, when, title, turns, tools, id. Default limit 10 | `sessions.ts`; `sessions-view.ts:49–73` |
| `dora sessions show <id>` | First 10 user turns, tool-name histogram, recent call inputs, skills invoked. Tokens hardcoded unavailable | `sessions/show.ts` |

`skill-classify.ts` does **not** read sessions. It classifies origin (authored / global / imported). Unused / remove *use* that origin plus session evidence.

### 4. Gaps vs agent-traces

| Gap | Doraval now |
| --- | --- |
| Per-event table | No. Grain is one `SessionPrimitives` blob |
| `is_error` / error_rate | Not extracted |
| Tokens (input/output/cache) on the blob | Not on primitives. Partial list-level tokens on Codex and Grok only |
| Cost | Never |
| Thinking / compaction / parent id | Not kept (Claude thinking blocks dropped; only `type === "text"` and `tool_use`) |
| Parquet / three-file export | No. No parquet in `package.json` |
| Hub corpora / `format:agent-traces` tag | No |
| Pi format | No |
| ATIF | No |
| Full-corpus (beyond 10 / 30d) | Review window is the product. `listSessions` default limit 10. `findSession` walks 50 |
| `user_messages` turn / normPos | No |

### 5. Existing seams

```11:17:src/core/session-adapters/types.ts
export interface SessionAdapter {
  agent: string;
  detect(): boolean;
  findLatestSession(cwd: string): string | null;
  listRecentSessions(cwd: string, limit?: number): SessionListItem[];
  parse(path: string): SessionPrimitives;
}
```

`parse` is the IR boundary. Review, unused, eval, and `sessions show` all consume `SessionPrimitives`. They do not read JSONL.

A deeper analysis layer **sits on top of** `SessionAdapter.parse` / `SessionPrimitives`. It does not replace adapters. Adapters own disk layout and format quirks (Claude project hash, Codex sqlite, Copilot db, Grok group dirs). Replacing `parse` would break `detectUsageInSession`, `collectSessionEvidence`, and `runEval`.

Extending the blob (tokens, errors, thinking) is additive. An event table is a **new** grain. It can be derived from the same files the adapters already open. It should not become the type that review matches against.

---

## C. Mapping

| Axis | agent-traces | Doraval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Format coverage** | Pi, Claude Code, Codex, ATIF. Detect from file bytes. Hub-first. | Claude Code, Grok, Cursor, Codex, Copilot. Detect from home dir. Project-cwd-first. |
| **Grain** | `Entry` → 3 tables (session / event / content). Legacy 44-col flat. | One `SessionPrimitives` per file. Tool list + string arrays. |
| **Analyses** | `tool_counts`, `token_stats`, `error_rate`, `summary`, durations, conversation view. Research-only health-predictor claim (no code). | Invoke evidence, review window 10/30d, unused / remove candidate, LLM adherence. Tool histogram on `sessions show`. |
| **Storage** | In-memory Polars. Export parquet (flat via CLI; 3 files via API). | Live agent logs on disk. No warehouse. 50 MB skip. |
| **Product job** | Research corpus: Hub datasets, cost, errors, training-data curation. | Evidence for context quality: did this Skill get used, should we remove it, did the agent follow it. |

**YAGNI — do not port Polars / Parquet / Python.** The review window is tens of files, not 500k Hub events (`agent.md:112`). Bun already has what those aggregates need if we want them later:

- `JSON.parse` + line split (`safeJsonParse` in `session-parse.ts:47–53`).
- `Map` / `Record` counts — already `toolCallCounts`.
- `Array.filter` / `reduce` for error fractions and token sums, once those fields exist.
- `Date` for duration (`durationMs` already optional).
- `bun:sqlite` — already how Codex and Copilot list sessions.
- No parquet reader/writer in `package.json`. Do not add one for this job.

---

## Grill questions

Do not answer these here.

1. Keep `SessionPrimitives` as the review IR, and add a separate event list only if a new analysis needs per-turn `is_error` / tokens — or widen the blob?
2. Stay inside the Review window (last 10, 30 days), or add a full-corpus path that walks every log the adapters can see?
3. Stay on local agent homes (`~/.claude`, `~/.grok`, …) only, or also ingest Hub `format:agent-traces` / ATIF / Pi files?
4. New `dora` verb for analysis, or deepen `dora sessions` / `dora review` / `dora skill unused`?
5. Extract tokens / cost / `is_error` inside each adapter (Claude usage, Codex sqlite `tokens_used`, Pi `usage.cost`), or leave them out until a caller asks?
6. Is Pi or ATIF a Doraval format at all, given no local installer and no Skill-invoke path?
7. Should `dora sessions show` stop printing `Tokens: unavailable` and use the Codex/Grok list-level token fields that already exist?
8. If we add an event grain, does `skillsInvoked` stay a session-level derived field (current product), or become a query over events?

1→---
name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
---

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline — challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill — that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

10→## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
20→│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/
30→│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── CONTEXT.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

40→Create files lazily — only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y — which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

50→When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account' — do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible — which is right?"

60→### Update CONTEXT.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up — capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).

`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

70→1. **Hard to reverse** — the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context** — a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off** — there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

1→---
name: grilling
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
---

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled — the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

10→Each question should be formatted like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree — settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

20→Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it — don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report — ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's — put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

1→# CONTEXT.md Format

## Structure

```md
# {Context Name}

{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}

10→## Language

**Order**:
{A one or two sentence description of the term}
_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction

**Invoice**:
A request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.
_Avoid_: Bill, payment request

20→**Customer**:
A person or organization that places orders.
_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account
```

## Rules

- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.
- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.
- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.
30→- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.

## Single vs multi-context repos

**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.

**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:

```md
# Context Map
40→
## Contexts

- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md) — receives and tracks customer orders
- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md) — generates invoices and processes payments
- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md) — manages warehouse picking and shipping

## Relationships

- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking
50→- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices
- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`
```

The skill infers which structure applies:

- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts
- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context
- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved

60→When multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.

1→# Doraval — domain context

Agent-readable glossary for architecture and code. Product language wins over legacy file names.

## Product

**Doraval** (`dora` / `doraval`) is a context-effectiveness CLI: scan, review, and manage agent skills, memory files, and rules across Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Grok.

## Core terms
10→
| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Skill** | A directory with `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + body) that agents load as specialized instructions. |
| **Authored** | Skill origin: a Skill under the current project. |
| **Global** | Skill origin: a Skill under the user home (for example `~/.claude/skills`). |
| **Imported** | Skill origin: a Skill from plugin cache or `node_modules`. Read-only. Not a remove target. |
| **Plugin** | A package that ships one or more Skills (and related files) for an agent. First-class. Not “a Skill folder”. |
| **Plugin-owned Skill** | A Skill that lives inside a Plugin. Detected when an ancestor has a Plugin manifest (`plugin.json` or the provider marketplace file). Not the same as **Imported**. This pass: `unused` skips it with no error; named `remove` / `restore` exit `1` and Next is `dora review --quick <plugin-root>`. Review and `fix` on that Skill path are a later pass. |
| **Subagent** | A specialized agent file (for example `.claude/agents/*.md`). Own role and tools. Not a Memory file. Not a Skill. |
20→| **Catalog (this pass)** | The artifact types this pass must treat: Skill, Plugin, Memory file, Subagent. Out of scope: hooks, channels, MCP, scheduled tasks, and the rest of `docs/research-notes`. |
| **Review** | One `review(path)`. Tiered quality pass over a Skill and/or Memory file: structure → heuristics → optional LLM judge → optional sessions. Workspace and Skill reviews also include cwd Memory files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `copilot-instructions.md`). |
| **Scan** | Fast workspace health check (`dora` bare): agents present, skill validation, shadows/overlaps, install/intelligence. |
| **Rule** | One module (`src/core/rules`). Registry, packages, resolve, stamp, and mutation. CLI only renders and writes config. |
| **Package** | Named enable-set of rules: `recommended` (default), `strict`, `minimal`. |
| **Judge** | One module (`judge()`). Owns mode (**api** / **delegate** / **fail**) and transport. Review passes prompt, schema, and `ci`. |
| **Memory** | Product term for principles, artifacts, and always-on files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, …) under `~/.doraval/memory/` and project roots. |
| **Config** | Global product config at `~/.doraval/config.yml`. Code type is still `JournalConfig` (legacy name — not a “journal product”). Holds projects, `eval.*` judge settings, rules, agent command. |

You are doing /research for Doraval at /Users/saif/Experiments/doraval.

## Question

What **analysis approaches** exist for agent session traces, and what must Doraval **Capture-wide** on an Event so a later Runner can suggest context-effectiveness improvements?

This is NOT a field-name scavenger hunt only. Compare inherent approaches: how they model a run, what they persist, what analyses they unlock, what they do not do.

Doraval already decided (see CONTEXT.md Session-analysis pass, still open):
- This pass = sharper evidence. Corpus / Later analyse later.
- Event grain: Session IR is a list of Events + derived Session summary. No Content table.
- Capture-wide: store facts now; CLI output stays evidence-only.
- Adopt-aggressively; breaking Review/unused/sessions is allowed.
- Stack stays Bun/TypeScript. Do not recommend porting Python/Polars/UI/SDK products.
- Sit on existing session adapters (Claude, Grok, Cursor, Codex, Copilot) that parse logs **after the fact**. Doraval does not wrap those agents with an SDK.

Read first:
- `/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval/CONTEXT.md` (Session, Event, Review window, Capture-wide, this pass)
- `/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval/docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md` (already done — CITE, do not re-derive)
- `/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval/src/core/session-parse.ts` and `src/core/session-adapters/types.ts` (what we already keep)

## Sources (primary only)

Clone or fetch. Record SHA / doc URL + date.

1. **agent-traces** (baseline, already noted): cite `docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md` and `/tmp/agent-traces-research` if still there (HEAD 63df641). Approach: post-hoc JSONL → tables. Do not re-read the whole tree unless you need one fact 48 missed.

2. **Rxflex/agenttrace** — https://github.com/Rxflex/agenttrace
   Clone shallow to `/tmp/rxflex-agenttrace-research`. Record HEAD.
   Read README, SDK span model, backend domain entities, ingest API. Approach: instrument-at-runtime + span tree + local SQLite + web debugger.
   What they persist (span types, parent, attributes, events, timing).
   What analyses the UI actually does vs roadmap (evals, run compare — README says not implemented).

3. **OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions**
   Primary: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai
   and https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/ (follow redirects).
   Clone the genai conventions repo if needed.
   Document: span operations (chat, execute_tool, invoke_agent), required attributes (model, tokens, provider), events vs span attributes, agent spans, parent/child, content capture (opt-in).
   Approach: standard span vocabulary for interoperability. Not a parser of Claude JSONL.

4. **ATIF** — Agent Trajectory Interchange Format
   Primary spec: https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md
   Also check current schema version in that repo if the RFC is stale.
   Related (only if needed to see what ATIF holds): vinhnx90/vtcode or harbor examples; atifact (waldekmastykarz/atifact) converts Claude/Copilot/Codex → ATIF — useful for “can our logs become ATIF?”
   Approach: interchange / trajectory JSON, not a live debugger.

5. **Langfuse**
   Official docs only: https://langfuse.com/docs (tracing, observations, sessions, scores).
   Approach: hosted observability + eval scores. What observation types (span, generation, event, tool). What they persist that post-hoc JSONL often lacks (user feedback, scores).
   Do not write a product review. Extract the data model.

6. **Entire**
   Doraval already has CLI-UX note `docs/research-notes/47-entire-cli-ux.md` — that is NOT the session model. Find Entire’s session / checkpoint / transcript model from:
   - https://github.com/entireio/cli (session, checkpoint commands and types)
   - Entire docs if first-party
   What they store vs analyse. Do they do context-effectiveness, or provenance/replay?

## What to extract per source

For each:
- Job in one sentence (debugger / corpus / interchange / evidence / provenance)
- How they model a run (flat events, span tree, trajectory steps, session+checkpoint)
- Facts they persist that Doraval SessionPrimitives does NOT
- Analyses they actually implement (not roadmap vapor)
- Whether they read **existing coding-agent JSONL** or require **SDK instrumentation**
- What Doraval can steal as an *approach* without stealing the stack

## Synthesis (the point)

A comparison table: source × job × model × post-hoc vs instrument × steal / skip.

Then a **Capture-wide Event checklist**: facts worth storing on a Doraval Event because two or more approaches use them AND our adapters can extract them from local logs (or clearly cannot — say so).

Group checklist as:
- Already on SessionPrimitives / adapters
- Available in our logs, not kept today (cite adapter file)
- Common in span/OTel/ATIF, **not** in Claude/Grok/Cursor/Codex/Copilot logs (do not invent)
- Later / skip (Hub, scores, SDK wrap, web UI)

End with **grill questions** unanswered (4–8). These feed the resumed grill. Include: parent/span tree vs flat seq; tokens/error/timing; skill-invoke as derived; Review window vs full corpus; ATIF export later?

## Output

Write ONE file:

`/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval/docs/research-notes/49-agent-trace-approaches.md`

Match sibling notes:
- Title: `# 49 Agent-trace analysis approaches`
- **Captured:** 2026-08-24
- **Status:** research only. Do not edit Doraval CLI from this file.
- Cite path:line or commit SHA URLs
- Short sentences. Tables. No fluff. STE100-ish.

Do NOT edit docs/research-notes.md
Do NOT commit
Do NOT touch src/

Return: path, SHAs, 6-bullet synthesis, sources you could not reach.
