FileContent.content:
1→# 49 Agent-trace analysis approaches

**Captured:** 2026-08-24
**Status:** research only. Do not edit Doraval CLI from this file.
**Product intent:** sharper Session evidence this pass. Store Capture-wide facts on an Event so a later Runner can suggest context-effectiveness improvements. Bun/TypeScript. Post-hoc adapters. No SDK wrap. No Python/Polars/UI port.

Cite sibling: [`48-agent-traces.md`](./48-agent-traces.md). Do not re-derive agent-traces.

---
10→
## Primary sources

| Source | Clone / URL | HEAD / date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agent-traces | `/tmp/agent-traces-research` · https://github.com/davanstrien/agent-traces | `63df6415bdd651c49d66f161665e000c5c6d94f2` (note 48, 2026-08-24) |
| Rxflex/agenttrace | `/tmp/rxflex-agenttrace-research` · https://github.com/Rxflex/agenttrace | `012f137782cb576ce461b8b6523d2c5a16ba698a` (“docs: add star history chart to README”) |
| OTel GenAI conventions | `/tmp/otel-semconv-genai-research` · https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai | `56d6b11a02129319bf371083fa134b7ce989c976` |
| OTel published docs | https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/ | 2026-08-24. Hub page **moved**; used clone + `gen-ai-spans.md` / `gen-ai-agent-spans.md` / `gen-ai-events.md` |
| ATIF | `/tmp/harbor-research` · https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor | `f633b8a8bca427ee426ff22b182a9dc2cc50e1d4` |
20→| ATIF RFC | `rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md` | Active. Changelog **v1.7**. Harbor Pydantic default `ATIF-v1.7` (`src/harbor/models/trajectories/trajectory.py:15–26`) |
| atifact (convert only) | `/tmp/atifact-research` · https://github.com/waldekmastykarz/atifact | `db0bf0fcac29adc26778185383d42f2d7c8ceba6` |
| Langfuse | Official docs only. No clone. | 2026-08-24: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/data-model · observation-types · sessions · evaluation/overview |
| Entire | `/tmp/entire-cli-research` · https://github.com/entireio/cli | `91a7fd7fcb3d6990537d5a8f9235d05b8e6fad10` (same clone as note 47) |

Doraval read: `CONTEXT.md` Session-analysis pass; `src/core/session-parse.ts`; `src/core/session-adapters/{types,claude,grok,cursor,codex,copilot}.ts`.

Did not edit `src/`. Did not commit. Did not edit `docs/research-notes.md`.

---
30→
## Inherent approaches (not products)

Five jobs. They disagree on **when** they see a run and **what** they persist.

| Approach | When they see the run | Model of a run | Persist | Unlock | Do not do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Post-hoc tables** (agent-traces) | After the agent wrote JSONL | Flat `Entry` → sessions + events (+ content view) | Columns: type, seq, tokens, error, parent_id, tool | Corpus counts: tools, tokens, error rate, duration | Skill unused. No live debugger. No scores. |
| **Instrument + span tree** (AgentTrace, OTel, Langfuse) | During the call | Tree: parent span → children. Timing is first-class | Span id, parent, start/end, attributes, events | Waterfall, nested tool/LLM, live status | Cannot read Claude JSONL unless someone wraps the agent |
| **Trajectory interchange** (ATIF) | After, or as the harness writes | Ordered **steps** (user / agent / system). Tool call + observation pair | `tool_call_id`, metrics, context-management, subagent refs | Replay, SFT/RL, export across tools | Not a debugger. Not a warehouse. |
40→| **Evidence / invoke** (Doraval today) | After. Local agent homes | One `SessionPrimitives` blob per file | Tools, user/assistant text, `skillsInvoked` | Review window, unused, adherence | Per-event tokens/error. Tree. Cost. |
| **Provenance / checkpoint** (Entire) | During (hooks) + after (`import`) | Session → checkpoints → compacted transcript | Git state, tokens, skill events, rewind | Replay, recap, token advice | Skill unused. Context-effectiveness as Doraval means it |

Doraval sits on **post-hoc + evidence**. Capture-wide means: take Event facts from the first three so Later analyse can grow. Do not become the last two products.

---

## 1. agent-traces — post-hoc JSONL → tables

**Job:** corpus parse. Behavioral counts, cost, errors, training-data curation.
50→
**Model:** JSONL line → `Entry` → three tables. Session row + event row + content row. `seq` = rank of line within `session_id`. `parentId` stored. Not walked.

**Cite:** note 48. Code `/tmp/agent-traces-research/agent_traces/dataset.py:22–73`, `parser.py:164–226`.

**Analyses that exist:** `tool_counts`, `token_stats`, `error_rate`, `session_durations`, `summary`. No predictor (note 48 §9).

**Post-hoc.** File bytes or Hub. No SDK.

**Facts we do not keep:** per-event `seq`, `type`, `parent_id`, `is_error`, `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_read`, `cost_total`, `stop_reason`, thinking, `exit_code`. Claude usage is on `message.usage` (`parser.py:414–419`).
60→
**Steal:** Event list + derived Session summary. Two grains. No Content table (CONTEXT already). Tokens / error / seq on the Event.

**Skip:** Polars, Parquet, Hub, Pi, ATIF ingest this pass.

---

## 2. Rxflex/agenttrace — instrument + local debugger

**Job:** local step-by-step debugger for a Python agent you own.
70→
**Model:** `AgentRun` + `TraceNode` tree + `SpanEvent` list.

Span types (`backend/src/agent_trace/domain/value_objects/span_type.py:7–10`):

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `agent_run` | Root of one execution |
| `step` | Generic unit of work |
| `tool_call` | One tool |
80→| `llm_call` | One model call |

Each node: `id`, `run_id`, `parent_id`, `name`, `span_type`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `attributes` JSON. Duration = end − start (`trace_node.py:40–45`).

Events on a node: `event_type` + `payload`. SDK uses `input` / `output` / `error` (`sdk/.../span.py:89–94`). Exception on `__exit__` writes an error event (`span.py:129–133`).

Ingest: `POST /api/v1/ingest/events` with `run_id` + `{type: span_start|span_end|span_event, data}` (`application/dto/schemas.py:32–85`; `ingest.py:12`). SQLite tables `runs`, `trace_nodes`, `span_events` (`infrastructure/database/models.py`).

**UI actually does:** run list (name, timestamps, duration, status running/completed/failed). Expandable tree. Details: type, timing, attributes JSON, events. No filter. No search. No waterfall (roadmap). Source: `README.md:238–261`; frontend `RunList` + `TraceTree` + `DetailsPanel`. Grep of `frontend/` found no eval / compare / score code.

90→**Roadmap, not shipped** (`README.md:298–322`): LangChain/OpenAI wrappers, timeline, filter, **run compare**, **evaluations**, Postgres, JSON export.

**Requires SDK instrumentation.** Does not parse Claude / Grok / Cursor / Codex / Copilot JSONL.

**Steal:** Event has `id`, optional `parent_id`, `started_at` / `ended_at` (or `durationMs`), `type` enum close to message/tool/llm, `is_error` as an event or flag. Tree is a **view** over a flat list with parent ids. AgentTrace already stores flat then `TreeBuilder.build_tree` (`domain/services/tree_builder.py:20–67`).

**Skip:** Python SDK wrap, FastAPI, React debugger, SQLite warehouse.

---

100→## 3. OpenTelemetry GenAI — span vocabulary

**Job:** standard names so many backends can read one instrumented run.

**Model:** spans + optional events + metrics. Not a parser of coding-agent JSONL.

**Status:** Development. Clone docs 2026-08-24. Published `/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/` hub is a **Moved** page; content lives on child pages.

## 4. ATIF — trajectory interchange

**Job:** one JSON document that debugging, SFT, and RL can share.
160→
**Model:** root Trajectory + ordered `steps[]`. Not a span tree. Not a live run.

A **step** is one system prompt, one user message, or one agent turn (LLM + tool_calls + observation). `step_id` starts at 1. `source` ∈ `system` | `user` | `agent`.

RFC: `/tmp/harbor-research/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md` (Active, April 2026, changelog v1.7). Harbor default schema `ATIF-v1.7`.

### Persist (v1.7)

Root: `schema_version`, optional `session_id` (run-scoped), optional `trajectory_id` (document-scoped), required `agent` (name + version), `steps`, optional `final_metrics`, `continued_trajectory_ref`, `subagent_trajectories`, `extra`.
170→
Step: `step_id`, `timestamp`, `source`, `model_name`, `message`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls[]` (`tool_call_id`, `function_name`, `arguments`), `observation.results[]` (`source_call_id`, `content`, `is_error` not first-class — extra), `metrics` (prompt/completion/cached tokens, `cost_usd`, optional token ids / logprobs), `llm_call_count`, `is_copied_context`.

**Context management** (Section VII, RFC lines 572–612): system step `extra.context_management` `{type: compaction|pruning|injection, boundary: replace|append|truncate}`. After `boundary=replace`, later context is the observation summary + new turns. Pre-boundary steps stay for audit.

### Analyses ATIF itself implements

None. It is a format. Harbor writes it during trials and validates with Pydantic. Harbor `analyze/` is task/rubric, not generic session analysis.

## 4. ATIF — trajectory interchange

**Job:** one JSON document that debugging, SFT, and RL can share.
160→
**Model:** root Trajectory + ordered `steps[]`. Not a span tree. Not a live run.

A **step** is one system prompt, one user message, or one agent turn (LLM + tool_calls + observation). `step_id` starts at 1. `source` ∈ `system` | `user` | `agent`.

RFC: `/tmp/harbor-research/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md` (Active, April 2026, changelog v1.7). Harbor default schema `ATIF-v1.7`.

### Persist (v1.7)

Root: `schema_version`, optional `session_id` (run-scoped), optional `trajectory_id` (document-scoped), required `agent` (name + version), `steps`, optional `final_metrics`, `continued_trajectory_ref`, `subagent_trajectories`, `extra`.
170→
Step: `step_id`, `timestamp`, `source`, `model_name`, `message`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls[]` (`tool_call_id`, `function_name`, `arguments`), `observation.results[]` (`source_call_id`, `content`, `is_error` not first-class — extra), `metrics` (prompt/completion/cached tokens, `cost_usd`, optional token ids / logprobs), `llm_call_count`, `is_copied_context`.

**Context management** (Section VII, RFC lines 572–612): system step `extra.context_management` `{type: compaction|pruning|injection, boundary: replace|append|truncate}`. After `boundary=replace`, later context is the observation summary + new turns. Pre-boundary steps stay for audit.

### Analyses ATIF itself implements

None. It is a format. Harbor writes it during trials and validates with Pydantic. Harbor `analyze/` is task/rubric, not generic session analysis.

### Can our logs become ATIF?
180→
**Yes for Claude, Copilot, Codex.** atifact (`db0bf0fc`) converts those JSONL (and HAR) → ATIF-v1.7. **Steal:** tool_call_id + observation join. Step source. Metrics block. Compaction as a typed system Event. `is_copied_context` if a log marks compact/summary. Session summary = `final_metrics`.

| **Instrument + span tree** (AgentTrace, OTel, Langfuse) | During the call | Tree: parent span → children. Timing is first-class | Span id, parent, start/end, attributes, events | Waterfall, nested tool/LLM, live status | Cannot read Claude JSONL unless someone wraps the agent |
| **Trajectory interchange** (ATIF) | After, or as the harness writes | Ordered **steps** (user / agent / system). Tool call + observation pair | `tool_call_id`, metrics, context-management, subagent refs | Replay, SFT/RL, export across tools | Not a debugger. Not a warehouse. |
| **Evidence / invoke** (Doraval today) | After. Local agent homes | One `SessionPrimitives` blob per file | Tools, user/assistant text, `skillsInvoked` | Review window, unused, adherence | Per-event tokens/error. Tree. Cost. |
| **Provenance / checkpoint** (Entire) | During (hooks) + after (`import`) | Session → checkpoints → compacted transcript | Git state, tokens, skill events, rewind | Replay, recap, token advice | Skill unused. Context-effectiveness as Doraval means it |

Doraval sits on **post-hoc + evidence**. Capture-wide means: take Event facts from the first three so Later analyse can grow. Do not become the last two products.

## 1. agent-traces — post-hoc JSONL → tables

**Job:** corpus parse. Behavioral counts, cost, errors, training-data curation.

**Model:** JSONL line → `Entry` → three tables. Session row + event row + content row. `seq` = rank of line within `session_id`. `parentId` stored. Not walked.

**Cite:** note 48. Code `/tmp/agent-traces-research/agent_traces/dataset.py:22–73`, `parser.py:164–226`.

**Analyses that exist:** `tool_counts`, `token_stats`, `error_rate`, `session_durations`, `summary`. No predictor (note 48 §9).

**Post-hoc.** File bytes or Hub. No SDK.

**Facts we do not keep:** per-event `seq`, `type`, `parent_id`, `is_error`, `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_read`, `cost_total`, `stop_reason`, thinking, `exit_code`. Claude usage is on `message.usage` (`parser.py:414–419`).

**Steal:** Event list + derived Session summary. Two grains. No Content table (CONTEXT already). Tokens / error / seq on the Event.

**Skip:** Polars, Parquet, Hub, Pi, ATIF ingest this pass.

## 2. Rxflex/agenttrace — instrument + local debugger

**Job:** local step-by-step debugger for a Python agent you own.

**Model:** `AgentRun` + `TraceNode` tree + `SpanEvent` list.

Span types (`backend/src/agent_trace/domain/value_objects/span_type.py:7–10`):

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `agent_run` | Root of one execution |
| `step` | Generic unit of work |
| `tool_call` | One tool |
| `llm_call` | One model call |

Each node: `id`, `run_id`, `parent_id`, `name`, `span_type`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `attributes` JSON. Duration = end − start (`trace_node.py:40–45`).

Events on a node: `event_type` + `payload`. SDK uses `input` / `output` / `error` (`sdk/.../span.py:89–94`). Exception on `__exit__` writes an error event (`span.py:129–133`).

Ingest: `POST /api/v1/ingest/events` with `run_id` + `{type: span_start|span_end|span_event, data}` (`application/dto/schemas.py:32–85`; `ingest.py:12`). SQLite tables `runs`, `trace_nodes`, `span_events` (`infrastructure/database/models.py`).

**UI actually does:** run list (name, timestamps, duration, status running/completed/failed). Expandable tree. Details: type, timing, attributes JSON, events. No filter. No search. No waterfall (roadmap). Source: `README.md:238–261`; frontend `RunList` + `TraceTree` + `DetailsPanel`. Grep of `frontend/` found no eval / compare / score code.

**Roadmap, not shipped** (`README.md:298–322`): LangChain/OpenAI wrappers, timeline, filter, **run compare**, **evaluations**, Postgres, JSON export.

**Requires SDK instrumentation.** Does not parse Claude / Grok / Cursor / Codex / Copilot JSONL.

**Steal:** Event has `id`, optional `parent_id`, `started_at` / `ended_at` (or `durationMs`), `type` enum close to message/tool/llm, `is_error` as an event or flag. Tree is a **view** over a flat list with parent ids. AgentTrace already stores flat then `TreeBuilder.build_tree` (`domain/services/tree_builder.py:20–67`).

**Skip:** Python SDK wrap, FastAPI, React debugger, SQLite warehouse.

## 3. OpenTelemetry GenAI — span vocabulary

**Job:** standard names so many backends can read one instrumented run.

**Model:** spans + optional events + metrics. Not a parser of coding-agent JSONL.

**Status:** Development. Clone docs 2026-08-24. Published `/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/` hub is a **Moved** page; content lives on child pages.

### Operations (`gen_ai.operation.name`)

Well-known values on agent spans (`docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md:127–148`):

`chat` · `create_agent` · `embeddings` · `execute_tool` · `generate_content` · `invoke_agent` · `invoke_workflow` · `plan` · `retrieval` · `text_completion` · plus memory ops.

Doraval Event types need only a subset: **message (chat)** · **execute_tool** · **invoke_agent** (subagent / Skill) · error.

### Required / recommended attributes (inference)

From `docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md:64–105`:

| Attr | Level | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gen_ai.operation.name` | Required | What happened |
| `gen_ai.provider.name` | Required | Vendor flavor |
| `error.type` | Conditionally required on error | Class of failure |
| `gen_ai.request.model` | Conditionally required | Model asked |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | Conditionally required if the library already has one | Session/thread. **Do not invent a UUID** (note [5], lines 138–151) |
| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` | Recommended | Prompt / completion. Input includes cache |
| `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` / `cache_write.input_tokens` | Recommended when applicable | Cache split |
| `gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens` | Recommended when applicable | Thinking tokens |
| `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` | Recommended | Why the model stopped |
| `gen_ai.conversation.compacted` | Recommended when known | Context compaction happened. Set `true` only; leave unset otherwise |
| `gen_ai.input.messages` / `output.messages` / `system_instructions` / `tool.definitions` | **Opt-In** | Full content. PII warning |

### Agent / tool spans

- `invoke_agent` — CLIENT (remote) or INTERNAL (in-process). Name: `invoke_agent {agent.name}`.
- `execute_tool` — INTERNAL. Name: `execute_tool {tool.name}`. Required: `operation.name`, `tool.name`. Recommended: `tool.call.id`. Opt-in: arguments + result (`gen-ai-spans.md:1102–1146`).
- Parent/child is the OTel span tree. Conversation id groups spans. Not the same as parent span id.

### Events vs span attributes

Events (`docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-events.md`):

- `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` — opt-in dump of inputs/outputs **independent of traces**.
- `gen_ai.evaluation.result` — eval score on a span.

Content may live on span attributes **or** on those events. Both are opt-in. Errors use span status + `error.type`.

**Post-hoc?** No. Needs an SDK or auto-instrumentation in the agent process. Claude Code JSONL is not an OTel export.

**Steal:** field names and requirement levels. `conversation.id` = our `sessionId` when the log already has it. Tokens + `error.type` + tool call id + compaction flag. Do not invent ids. Do not require provider enum this pass (`anthropic` is derivable from Claude model names; Cursor/Copilot often have no provider).

**Skip:** emit OTel from Doraval. Wrap agents. Metrics backend.

## 4. ATIF — trajectory interchange

**Job:** one JSON document that debugging, SFT, and RL can share.

**Model:** root Trajectory + ordered `steps[]`. Not a span tree. Not a live run.

A **step** is one system prompt, one user message, or one agent turn (LLM + tool_calls + observation). `step_id` starts at 1. `source` ∈ `system` | `user` | `agent`.

RFC: `/tmp/harbor-research/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md` (Active, April 2026, changelog v1.7). Harbor default schema `ATIF-v1.7`.

### Persist (v1.7)

Root: `schema_version`, optional `session_id` (run-scoped), optional `trajectory_id` (document-scoped), required `agent` (name + version), `steps`, optional `final_metrics`, `continued_trajectory_ref`, `subagent_trajectories`, `extra`.

Step: `step_id`, `timestamp`, `source`, `model_name`, `message`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls[]` (`tool_call_id`, `function_name`, `arguments`), `observation.results[]` (`source_call_id`, `content`, `is_error` not first-class — extra), `metrics` (prompt/completion/cached tokens, `cost_usd`, optional token ids / logprobs), `llm_call_count`, `is_copied_context`.

**Context management** (Section VII, RFC lines 572–612): system step `extra.context_management` `{type: compaction|pruning|injection, boundary: replace|append|truncate}`. After `boundary=replace`, later context is the observation summary + new turns. Pre-boundary steps stay for audit.

### Analyses ATIF itself implements

None. It is a format. Harbor writes it during trials and validates with Pydantic. Harbor `analyze/` is task/rubric, not generic session analysis.

### Can our logs become ATIF?

**Yes for Claude, Copilot, Codex.** atifact (`db0bf0fc`) converts those JSONL (and HAR) → ATIF-v1.7. Claude parser pairs `tool_use` with later `tool_result` via pending step (`src/parsers/claude-code.ts:162–219`). Reads `message.usage`, `result.total_cost_usd`, `is_error` on tool_result, `parent_tool_use_id` (skips Task subagent lines). **No Grok. No Cursor.**

**Steal:** tool_call_id + observation join. Step source. Metrics block. Compaction as a typed system Event. `is_copied_context` if a log marks compact/summary. Session summary = `final_metrics`.

**Skip:** emit ATIF this pass (grill). Token ids / logprobs (not in local coding-agent logs we keep). RL fields.

## 5. Langfuse — hosted obs + scores

**Job:** production observability + evaluation. Not a local JSONL parser.

**Model:** Session → Trace → Observation (nested). Docs store **one observations table**; each row copies trace-level `user_id` / `session_id` / tags / metadata.

Cite: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/data-model (2026-08-24).

### Observation types

https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/observation-types :

`event` · `span` · `generation` · `agent` · `tool` · `chain` · `retriever` · `evaluator` · `embedding` · `guardrail`.

A **generation** holds prompts, token usage, cost. A **tool** is one action. An **agent** orchestrates tools.

**Session** = optional group of traces that share `sessionId` (US-ASCII, < 200 chars). Chat thread. https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/sessions

### Scores (what JSONL lacks)

Scores attach to Trace, Observation, Session, or DatasetRun. Types: NUMERIC, CATEGORICAL, BOOLEAN, TEXT. Source: annotation UI, user feedback, SDK/API, LLM-as-judge. Cite: evaluation overview + scores search snippets 2026-08-24 (`/docs/evaluation/overview`, `/docs/evaluation/scores/data-model`).

**Built on OpenTelemetry.** Requires instrumentation (SDK or framework callback). Background batch + `flush()` for short-lived CLIs.

**Steal:** Event.type vocabulary (message / tool / generation). Scores as a **later attach** on Session or Event — not a Capture-wide required field. Session id grouping we already have.

**Skip:** hosted product, user-feedback widget, dataset experiments, OTel exporter this pass.

## 6. Entire — session + checkpoint + transcript

**Job:** provenance and replay of a coding session. Not context-effectiveness as Doraval defines it (Skill unused / remove candidate / adherence).

Note 47 is CLI UX only. Session model is here.

**Model:**

```
Session (unit of work)
  └─ Checkpoints (ephemeral shadow-branch + persistent metadata)
       └─ Compacted transcript.jsonl  + TokenUsage  + SkillEvent[]
```

Cite: `/tmp/entire-cli-research/docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`. Types: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session.go:15–51`; live state `cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:99+`; compact format `cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact/compact.go:25–80`.

**How they get data:** **hooks at runtime** (TurnStart / TurnEnd / SessionStop / Compaction) **and** `entire import` of existing agent transcripts (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, Pi). Import is post-hoc. Normal path is wrap-with-hooks.

**Store:**

| Fact | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Session id, agent, model, branch, phase (active/idle/ended) | `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` |
| TokenUsage: input, cache write/read, output, API call count, nested subagent | checkpoint + session state (`agent/types/token_usage.go`) |
| SkillEvent: name, signal, confidence, transcript_anchor, collapse | checkpoint metadata (`agent/types/skill_events.go`) |
| Compacted line: `v`, agent, cli_version, type, ts, id, input_tokens, output_tokens, content; tool_use **inlines result.status** (`error` / ok) | `transcript.jsonl` |
| Git tree / rewind | ephemeral + persistent stores |

**Analyses that exist (not roadmap):**

- `entire session list|info|current|tokens` — identity, transcript dump, token report.
- Token recommendations (`session_tokens.go:68–76`, `298–328`): cache-read ≥ 80% of volume → `context-replay-hotspot`; API calls ≥ 20 → `api-call-amplification`; long session (turns ≥ 10 or checkpoints ≥ 5); context window ≥ 80%. **This is token-pressure advice, not Skill-effectiveness.**
- Recap: counts of sessions / checkpoints / tokens (`recap/me_recap.go`).
- Rewind / resume / explain: provenance.

They do **not** compute Never invoked / Remove candidate. They record skill events so a UI can collapse verbose skill dumps.

**Steal:** pair tool result onto the tool Event (`result.status`). Keep tokens on Event when the log has them. Skill invoke as a **derived** record with source/signal (Entire already separates `SkillEvent` from raw transcript). Compaction as a session Event (`EventCompaction` in `session/phase.go:61`).

**Skip:** git checkpoints, hook wrap, Entire transcript format, TUI recap. Doraval does not become a rewind product.

## Comparison

| Source | Job | Model | Post-hoc vs instrument | Steal | Skip |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent-traces | corpus | Flat events + session row | Post-hoc JSONL / Hub | Event grain; seq; tokens; is_error | Polars, Hub, Content table |
| AgentTrace | debugger | Span tree + events | **Instrument** SDK | parent_id; start/end; error event; tree as view | SDK, UI, SQLite |
| OTel GenAI | interchange vocab | Span tree + opt-in content events | **Instrument** | operation / model / provider / tokens / error.type / tool.call.id / compacted | Emit OTel; wrap agents |
| ATIF | interchange / SFT | Trajectory steps | Write-time or convert | step source; tool_call_id↔result; metrics; compaction | ATIF file this pass; RL fields |
| Langfuse | hosted obs + eval | Session → trace → observation | **Instrument** | type enum; scores later | Hosted; feedback; experiments |
| Entire | provenance / replay | Session + checkpoint + transcript | Hooks **and** import | result status; token pressure facts; skill-event derived | Checkpoints; hook wrap |
| Doraval today | evidence | SessionPrimitives blob | Post-hoc adapters | Keep adapters; lift to Event list | Stay a blob |

**Two-or-more agreement** (the Capture-wide bar):

Every source that models a run keeps **identity** (session/run id), **order** (seq or step_id or start time), **kind** (user / assistant / tool / system), **tool name**, and **time** if the producer has it.

Four of six keep **tokens** (agent-traces, OTel, ATIF, Entire, Langfuse generations). Four keep **error** (agent-traces `is_error`, AgentTrace error event, OTel `error.type`, ATIF/atifact tool_result `is_error`, Entire `result.status`). Three keep **parent / call id** to join a tool to its result (OTel `tool.call.id`, ATIF `tool_call_id`, AgentTrace `parent_id`, Claude `uuid`/`parentUuid` / `tool_use.id`).

None of the instrumented products read Grok or Cursor JSONL. Only Doraval + Entire-import do.

## What this means for Doraval Event

Minimum Capture-wide Event (facts two or more approaches use **and** at least one adapter can fill):

```
sessionId
seq                 // 0-based order in file
type                // user | assistant | tool_call | tool_result | system | error
timestamp?          // ISO if present
id?                 // uuid / tool_use.id
parentId?           // parentUuid / parent_tool_use_id
toolName?
toolCallId?         // join result → call
input?              // tool args; keep small
output?             // tool result text; or skip body, keep isError
isError?
model?
inputTokens?
outputTokens?
cacheReadTokens?
stopReason?
```

Session **summary** (derived, not a second grain of truth):

```
counts: users, assistants, tools, errors
token totals (sum of events + list-level fallback)
durationMs (max−min timestamp, or Claude result/system)
skillsInvoked          // still derived
```

`skillsInvoked` stays **derived** (Claude Skill tool + attribution + command-name + Grok titles). Do not invent a native “skill span” the logs do not have.

CLI this pass: still Review / unused / `dora sessions`. Do not dump the Event list into `dora review`.

## Grill questions

Do not answer these here.

1. **Tree vs flat.** Store `parentId` and keep the IR a **list** (AgentTrace `TreeBuilder` view), or require a span tree in the type? Claude has parents. Grok/Cursor/Copilot do not.
2. **Tokens / error / timing.** Fill Event fields when the log has them (Claude usage + tool_result `is_error`; Grok/Codex list totals on the summary). Leave others unset. Or wait for a caller?
3. **Skill invoke.** Keep `skillsInvoked` as a Session derived field (current product + Entire SkillEvent). Or also emit a synthetic `type=skill` Event?
4. **Review window vs corpus.** Stay last 10 / 30 days for Review. Add a full walk only when Later analyse exists?
5. **ATIF export later?** atifact already maps Claude/Copilot/Codex → ATIF-v1.7. Do we emit ATIF from our Event list, shell out, or never?
6. **Tool result pairing.** Capture-wide: keep `toolCallId` + `tool_result` Events so error rate works. Inline result onto the call (Entire compact) as a view only?
7. **Cursor / Copilot skills.** Derive `skillsInvoked` like Claude (tool name / path / slash), or leave `[]` until a log field is proven?
8. **Token-pressure advice.** Entire `session tokens` recommendations are not Skill-effectiveness. Is that Later analyse, or out of product?

- kind (`type`)
- time
- tool name
- tool id + result + `isError`
- tokens when the file has them

last_assistant_message:
This choice is about **links**, not about Review output.

A Session is a list of Events in file order. That already gives “what happened next.” A **parent** says “this Event belongs under that Event” (a tool result under a tool call, a subagent under a Task).

Claude writes those links (`parentUuid`, `parent_tool_use_id`). Grok, Cursor, and Copilot do not. Order is all they have.

---

**A. Flat list. Drop `parentId`.**

Pros:
- Smallest type.
- Every adapter looks the same.
- Review and unused do not need parents.

Cons:
- You throw away a fact Claude already writes.
- Later you cannot join a tool result to its call except by guessing order.
- A subagent Task and its children become one mixed stream.

Use A if you believe pairing will always be “next line after the tool.” That is false when a Task nests, or two tools run in one turn.

---

**B. Flat list. Store `parentId` when the log has it. Tree is a later view.**

Pros:
- Capture-wide: keep the fact, do not invent it.
- IR stays a list. Review can ignore `parentId`.
- Later analyse can build a tree only for Claude (and any future log that has parents).
- Matches AgentTrace: store flat, `TreeBuilder` later.
- Matches ATIF: `tool_call_id` ↔ result, not a required tree type.

Cons:
- Some Events have `parentId`. Some do not. Callers must allow unset.
- You write one extra optional field now that this pass’s CLI will not print.

Use B if the log is the source of truth. Missing parent means “unknown,” not “root.”

---

**C. Require a span tree in the type.**

Pros:
- One shape for Later analyse. Walk children. Waterfall. Nested tools.

Cons:
- Grok, Cursor, and Copilot have no parents. You must invent them.
- Invented parents are not in the file. They will be wrong when two tools interleave.
- OpenTelemetry says do not invent conversation ids. Same rule for parents.
- Review and unused then sit on a fake tree.

Use C only if you wrap agents with an SDK. We already said we will not.

---

A concrete case:

Claude: user asks to research, agent starts Task (subagent), Task calls `grep`, `grep` errors.

- **A** — you see: Task, grep, error. You do not know the error belongs to grep inside Task.
- **B** — Claude’s ids say: error → grep → Task. Grok sessions stay a flat list.
- **C** — you invent a tree for Grok. That tree is a guess.

---

I still suggest **B**.

It keeps Claude’s links. It does not fake links for the other agents. A tree remains a view you can add when Later analyse needs it.

Reply with A, B, or C. If you still do not care, say **B** and we move on.

- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)

A description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.

Any further notes about the feature.

FileContent.content:
1→# Skill remove

Grill settled 2026-08-21. ADR 0006. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Remove candidate, Never invoked, Recent install, Quarantine, Explicit remove).

Seams (please confirm): **one new Remove planner** (predicate, name resolve, remove/restore plan) + **existing spawn-CLI** (help, write gate, Next, exits). Planner reuses session invoke matching, origin classify, Review window, and the write-gate helpers. No third seam.

## Problem Statement

Skills pile up. A Reader cannot see which ones this project has not invoked in a long time. Review already says **Never invoked**, but it does not recommend remove, and nothing in the CLI removes a Skill. A Runner has no safe write verb. Deleting a Global Skill from one repo’s Sessions would be a false remove. A Skill installed yesterday looks unused and must not be recommended.
10→
## Solution

Review and Scan recommend only a **Remove candidate**: an Authored Skill that is Never invoked in the Review window and is not a Recent install. A new rule (not R029) carries that Finding. Next points at `dora skill remove`.

`dora skill remove` deletes Authored Skills and Quarantines Global Skills. A name is enough. `--for` selects the agent. `--global` selects origin when the name clashes. One match: just Remove. Several matches: TTY picker; a Runner must pass `--for`, `--global`, or a path, or exit `2` with Next.

A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from this project’s Sessions (ADR 0006). The user can still name it (Explicit remove). That path Quarantines.

`dora skill restore` puts a Quarantined Global Skill back. Authored deletes come back with git. Occupied original path: stop.
20→
Reader and Runner see the same facts. Two voices. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run` to write.

## User Stories

1. As a Reader, I want Review to tell me which Authored Skills are Remove candidates, so that I know what is safe to drop.
2. As a Reader, I want Scan to show a count of Remove candidates and a Next line, so that bare `dora` leads to cleanup.
3. As a Runner, I want the Remove-candidate Finding to include a Next line to `dora skill remove`, so that I can act without guessing.
4. As a Reader, I want Never invoked and Remove candidate to stay different, so that a yesterday install is not a remove hint.
5. As a Reader, I want a Recent install that was Never invoked to still show R029 only, so that I know it is unused but young.
30→6. As a Reader, I want a Remove candidate to show the new rule and not also R029, so that one Skill is not two remove-shaped Findings.
7. As a Reader, I want an invoked Authored Skill to show no Remove-candidate Finding, so that live Skills stay quiet.
8. As a Reader, I want a Global Skill that this repo never invoked to stay off the recommend list, so that I do not delete a home Skill used elsewhere.
9. As a Reader, I want to still see that a Global Skill was Never invoked here (R029), so that I have the fact without a remove push.
10. As a Runner, I want Imported Skills refused for Remove, so that I do not break a plugin cache.
11. As a Reader, I want `dora skill remove` to list Remove candidates on a TTY when I pass no name, so that I can pick what to drop.
12. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill remove` without a name to exit `2` with Next, so that I am not hung on a picker.
13. As a Reader, I want to pass a Skill name and have it Removed when the name is unique, so that the common case is one command.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove foo --yes` to Remove a unique `foo`, so that I can script it.
15. As a Reader, I want `--for claude` to limit Remove to Claude’s copy, so that I do not touch Grok’s copy.
40→16. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when `foo` exists for more than one agent, so that I choose.
17. As a Runner, I want an ambiguous name without `--for` to exit `2` and name the agents, so that I can retry.
18. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when Claude has both Authored and Global `foo`, so that origin is not guessed.
19. As a Runner, I want `--global` (or a path) when Authored and Global share a name, so that I can disambiguate without a TTY.
20. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of an invoked Authored Skill I name, so that recommend is not the only door.
21. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Recent install I name, so that I can drop a Skill I just added and do not want.
22. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Global Skill I name, so that there is a way even though it is not a Remove candidate.
23. As a Reader, I want an Authored Remove to delete the Skill directory, so that git can bring it back.
24. As a Reader, I want a Global Remove to Quarantine, not delete, so that I can Restore.
25. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to keep the original path, agent, and time, so that Restore knows where to put it.
50→26. As a Reader, I want `dora skill restore foo` to put `foo` back at that original path, so that I undo a Global Remove.
27. As a Reader, I want bare `dora skill restore` on a TTY to pick from Quarantine, so that I do not remember names.
28. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill restore` to exit `2` with Next, so that I pass a name.
29. As a Reader, I want Restore to stop if the original path is occupied, so that I do not overwrite a reinstall.
30. As a Reader, I want Restore to refuse Authored deletes, so that I use git for those.
31. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove` and `dora skill restore` to be labeled **writes** on `dora agent-help`, so that I do not run them bare.
32. As a Runner, I want a detected agent without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I do not hang and I do not mutate.
33. As a Reader on a TTY, I want a confirm before delete or Quarantine, so that I get a beat.
34. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` to print the plan and write nothing, so that I can preview.
35. As a Runner, I want `--yes` to apply the plan, so that I can finish.
60→36. As a Runner, I want `--json` to emit the plan or the result, so that I can branch.
37. As a Reader, I want `dora skill --help` to list `remove` and `restore`, so that I find the verbs.
38. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove --help` to show name, `--for`, `--global`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and examples, so that I do not guess.
39. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help skill` (or `skill remove` / `skill restore`) to describe the write verbs, so that the live map is not stale.
40. As a Reader, I want Scan’s Next for Remove candidates to be `dora skill remove`, so that the hint and the command agree.
41. As a Reader, I want zero Remove candidates to produce no remove Next, so that a clean tree stays quiet.
42. As a Reader, I want a fresh clone (all SKILL.md mtimes young) to treat Authored Skills as Recent installs, so that we miss a recommend rather than push remove after checkout.
43. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove to still work after a fresh clone, so that I can drop a Skill I know I do not want.
44. As a Runner, I want an unknown name to exit `1` with Next `dora skill remove`, so that I recover.
45. As a Runner, I want Imported matches to be listed as refused, so that I know why nothing moved.
70→46. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to live under the Doraval home (honour `DORAVAL_HOME`), so that tests and machines do not collide.
47. As a Reader, I want Restore of a missing Quarantine name to say nothing is there, so that I am not told it restored.
48. As a CI job, I want `--ci` to imply JSON and no prompts, so that pipelines do not hang.
49. As a Reader, I want `--for` to use the same agent names as `dora new --for`, so that I do not learn a second flag language.
50. As a founder, I want no auto-delete, no Global recommend from one repo, no reuse of memory stash, and no `sdk-dx` API surface, so that v1 stays the grilled shape.
51. As a Runner, I want the new rule to be toggleable like other rules, so that a shop can turn the recommend off.
52. As a Reader, I want the new rule page generated with the catalog, so that the Finding’s docUrl works.
53. As a Reader, I want R029’s wording to stay “Never invoked”, so that we do not say unused.
54. As an implementer, I want one planner module for “is Remove candidate?”, “resolve name”, “plan Remove”, and “plan Restore”, so that CLI and Review/Scan do not fork the rules.
55. As an implementer, I want spawn-CLI tests for help, write gate, Next, and exits, so that Reader and Runner see the same contract as today.
80→56. As a Reader, I want a path argument to win when I pass one, so that I can point at a specific directory.

matches.content: Make every package in this repo a **deep module**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface. A package's public surface is its **entry points** — the files at the package root — and everything in its subfolders is hidden. This skill installs [dependency-cruiser](https://github.com/sverweij/dependency-cruiser) and the rules that make the entry points the only way in, then proves the rules bite.
## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"
description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.
- `.scratch/` — sign that a local-markdown issue tracker convention is already in use

> Explainer: The "issue tracker" is where issues live for this repo. Skills like `to-tickets`, `triage`, and `to-spec` read from and write to it — they need to know whether to call `gh issue create`, write a markdown file under `.scratch/`, or follow some other workflow you describe. Pick the place you actually track work for this repo.

The defaults are the five canonical roles, each label string equal to its name: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. On **yes**, write them as-is. Only if the user says no — usually because their tracker already uses other names (e.g. `bug:triage` for `needs-triage`) — collect the overrides so `triage` applies existing labels instead of creating duplicates.
For "other" issue trackers, write `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` from scratch using the user's description.

Tell the user the setup is complete and which engineering skills will now read from these files. Mention they can edit `docs/agents/*.md` directly later — re-running this skill is only necessary if they want to switch issue trackers or restart from scratch.

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

20→When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

30→Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

40→- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

1→# ADR Format

ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily — only when the first ADR is needed.

## Template

```md
10→# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}
```

That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why* — not in filling out sections.

## Optional sections

Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.
20→

# Session Event IR + Session health

Grill settled 2026-08-24. ADR 0007. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Session, Event, Capture-wide, Fill when present, Parent optional, Skill invoke record, Session health, Review window). Notes: `docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md`, `docs/research-notes/49-agent-trace-approaches.md`.

Seams (please confirm): **one Session load** (adapters emit Events; load derives Session summary, Skill invoke records, and Session health) + **existing spawn-CLI** (Review Session health block, unused, `dora sessions`). No third planner. No new verb.

## Problem Statement

A Reader and a Runner use Review and unused to improve context. Those commands see only a thin Session blob: tools, some text, a skill-name list. They cannot see tool errors, per-turn tokens, or cache-read share. Later we want Doraval to analyse Sessions and find gaps. The current blob cannot unlock that. `agent-traces` and Entire show what to keep (Events, tool pairs, derived skill records, token-pressure). We must not port Python, Polars, a debugger, or ATIF files this pass.

## Solution

Adapters parse each log into a list of **Events**. A **Session** summary and **Skill invoke records** are derived. Unused and Review read those records. Review adds a **Session health** block for token pressure (cache-read, call count, turn count) using Entire’s numbers. Session health is not a Finding.

The Review window stays last 10 Sessions and 30 days. Same verbs. No `dora analyse`. Fields that the log lacks stay unset. `parentId` is stored only when present. A tool is `tool_call` plus `tool_result`. ATIF is a later map, not an emit or ingest.

## User Stories

1. As a Runner, I want adapters to parse a Session into Events, so that later jobs have a real IR.
2. As a Runner, I want a derived Session summary (counts, token totals, duration, skills), so that Review and unused do not scan raw lines for identity.
3. As a Runner, I want unused to read Skill invoke records, so that Never invoked stays correct after the blob is gone.
4. As a Reader, I want Review to show a Session health block, so that I see token pressure next to Skill Findings.
5. As a Runner, I want Session health in Review JSON, so that I can branch without parsing a table.
6. As a Reader, I want Session health to be clearly not a Finding, so that I do not treat cache-read as a Skill defect.
7. As a Runner, I want unused to stay a Skill Finding (R034 / Never invoked), so that Session health does not replace remove logic.
8. As a Reader, I want cache-read ≥ 80% of known tokens to appear on Session health, so that I see Entire’s replay hotspot.
9. As a Reader, I want call count ≥ 20 to appear on Session health, so that I see Entire’s amplification signal.
10. As a Reader, I want user turns ≥ 10 to appear on Session health, so that I see a long Session.
11. As a Reader, I want no window-% or checkpoint signal, so that we do not invent Entire fields we cannot fill.
12. As a Reader, I want a Cursor Session with no tokens to omit the cache-read line, so that Fill when present holds.
13. As a Reader, I want a Session under all three thresholds to show a quiet Session health (no pressure), so that clean Sessions stay quiet.
14. As a Runner, I want Review window unchanged (10 / 30 days), so that unused does not flip on old logs.
15. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions` to still list the window, so that the list verb does not become a corpus walk.
16. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` to print tokens when known, so that “unavailable” is not a lie for Claude / Grok / Codex.
17. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` to still say tokens unavailable when unset, so that we do not invent zeros.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` not to dump every Event, so that Capture-wide does not become Review spam.
19. As a Runner, I want Claude `parentUuid` / tool ids stored as `parentId` / `id`, so that Later analyse can build a tree view.
20. As a Runner, I want Grok / Cursor / Copilot Events with unset `parentId`, so that we do not invent a span tree.
21. As a Runner, I want Claude `tool_use` and `tool_result` as two Events joined by `toolCallId`, so that `isError` has a home.
22. As a Runner, I want a tool_result with `is_error` to set `isError` on that Event, so that error rate is possible later.
23. As a Runner, I want usage tokens on the Event when Claude writes `message.usage`, so that cache-read share is real.
24. As a Runner, I want Grok / Codex list-level token totals on the Session summary when Events have none, so that we do not drop a total we already list.
25. As a Runner, I want cost on the Session summary only from Claude `result` (or equivalent), so that we do not invent dollars.
26. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for Claude Skill tool, so that unused still sees native invoke.
27. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for a slash command, so that Entire’s `prompt_slash_command` signal still counts.
28. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for Grok titles / SKILL.md paths, so that we do not drop a proven Grok signal.
29. As a Runner, I want Cursor / Codex / Copilot Skill invoke lists to stay empty unless a proven signal appears, so that we do not guess.
30. As a Runner, I want no Pi adapter, so that we do not add a format with no local Doraval home.
31. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record to name the signal and point at source Event id(s), so that we match Entire’s derived record.
32. As a Runner, I want no synthetic `type=skill` Event, so that the Event list stays a log projection.
33. As a Runner, I want path-in-tool-input matching to remain a fallback for unused if no Skill invoke record exists, so that we do not regress today’s path evidence.
34. As a Runner, I want Plugin-owned Skills to stay skipped by unused / remove, so that the Plugin-health pass does not regress.
35. As a Runner, I want session-eval to keep working, so that adherence judge still gets tool and user text.
36. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick` to still run without a judge, so that Session health does not require an LLM.
37. As a Runner, I want Scan to stay Skill health (no Session health block), so that Scan does not grow a second product.
38. As a Runner, I want no ATIF file written, so that we do not own schema drift this pass.
39. As a Runner, I want no ATIF ingest, so that we do not add a sixth source.
40. As a Runner, I want no Polars, Parquet, Hub, or Python sidecar, so that the stack stays Bun.
41. As a Runner, I want no new `dora analyse` / `dora plugin` verb, so that agent-help stays the same map plus Session health on Review.
42. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help review` to mention Session health as read-only Review output, so that the live map is not stale.
43. As a Reader, I want Review table to keep Skill Findings as they are, so that Session health is extra, not a rewrite of the Skill table.
44. As a Runner, I want Review JSON to add a `sessionHealth` object (not a Finding array row), so that clients do not treat it as R0xx.
45. As a Runner, I want `sessionHealth` to list which Sessions were considered (count, window), so that empty window is explicit.
46. As a Reader, I want zero Sessions in the window to say so on Session health, so that I do not read silence as “healthy.”
47. As a Runner, I want files over the existing size cap skipped, so that we do not change the 50 MB rule.
48. As an implementer, I want SessionPrimitives to become a derived view or to go away, so that parse is not two IRs.
49. As an implementer, I want one load function to be the only place that walks adapters, so that Review, unused, and sessions do not fork windows.
50. As an implementer, I want Event field unset (not 0) when missing, so that tests can tell “no tokens” from “zero tokens.”
51. As a Runner, I want `--json` and `--ci` on Review to include Session health without prompts, so that CI does not hang.
52. As a founder, I want Later analyse, Hub, scores, SDK wrap, and a web debugger out of this pass, so that we ship the IR and evidence only.

## Implementation Decisions

- Session IR is a list of Events plus a derived Session summary (ADR 0007).
- `SessionAdapter.parse` returns that Session (Events + summary). Callers do not read JSONL.
- Load still uses Review window constants (10, 30 days, 50 MB).
- Event fields (conceptual shape): `sessionId`, `seq`, `type` (`user` | `assistant` | `tool_call` | `tool_result` | `system` | `error`), optional `timestamp`, `id`, `parentId`, `toolName`, `toolCallId`, `input`, `output`, `isError`, `model`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `stopReason`.
- Missing log data → field omitted. Do not write 0, false, or a fake parent.
- Tool pair: two Events, same `toolCallId`. Inline join is not stored.
- Skill invoke record: `name`, `signal` (`skill_tool_use` | `prompt_slash_command` | Grok title/path signal), `eventIds`. Derived after parse. Not an Event type.
- Signals this pass: Claude Skill tool, slash command, Grok titles/paths. Cursor / Codex / Copilot: empty list.
- Unused and remove-candidate predicates read Skill invoke records first; keep path and `/name` mention as fallback so we do not regress.
- Session health is computed from loaded Events + summary. Not a rule. Not a Finding. Not on Scan.
- Thresholds: cache-read tokens / (input+output+cache-read) ≥ 0.8 when those fields exist; Event count of assistant + tool_call ≥ 20; `userTurnCount` ≥ 10.
- Review JSON: top-level `sessionHealth` with `window`, `sessionCount`, and a list of fired signals (code, sessionId, agent, detail). No `next` array added.
- Review text: a short Session health block after or before the Skill table. Next lines for Skills stay as they are.
- `dora sessions show`: print token totals when the summary has them; keep the rest of the current show (turns, tool histogram, skills). Do not print the full Event list.
- session-eval builds its prompt from the derived summary (tools, first user/assistant texts) so the judge contract stays.
- Plugin-owned skip on unused / remove is unchanged.
- No ATIF emit/ingest. No atifact. Event names stay ATIF-mappable.
- No new CLI verb. `agent-help` Review blurb mentions Session health.
- Write ADR 0007 in-repo (done at spec time).

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behaviour: given a fixture log, load returns the expected Events, summary, Skill invoke records, and Session health signals. Do not assert private helper names.
- Highest seam: Session load (inject adapters or fixture files). CLI seam: spawn Review / unused / sessions as today.
- Prior art: adapter `*.test.ts`, `session-evidence.test.ts`, `session-parse.test.ts`, `skill-remove` unused tests, Review CLI tests in `review.test.ts` and `test/cli.test.ts`.
- Cases that must exist: Claude fixture with usage + tool_result error + Skill tool; Grok fixture with title invoke and list tokens; Cursor fixture with tools and no tokens / no parents; empty window; under-threshold Session (no Session health fire); over-threshold Session (fires); unused still true/false after IR change; Plugin-owned unused skip unchanged; Review `--json` has `sessionHealth` and Findings stay Skill-shaped.
- Do not add a live Hub, ATIF, or AgentTrace docker test.

## Out of Scope

- New `dora analyse` (or corpus walk beyond the Review window)
- Content table as a grain
- Required span tree / invented parents
- ATIF emit or ingest; atifact dependency
- Pi adapter; Hub / `format:agent-traces`
- Polars, Parquet, Python sidecar, AgentTrace UI, OTel export, SDK wrap
- Langfuse scores / user thumbs
- Token-pressure as Skill Findings or Scan rows
- Context-window % and Entire checkpoints
- Thinking/PII body on Events (judge stays on assistant text)
- Changing Plugin-health, write gate, or agent-help read-only vs writes beyond Review’s Session health line
- Defining “gaps” for Later analyse

## Further Notes

- Capture-wide: store facts on Events now; CLI this pass stays Review / unused / sessions.
- Entire collapse flags are UI. Do not copy them.
- “Gaps” stays undefined. Later analyse is not this spec.
- Research: notes 48 and 49. Do not re-open the grill for field names unless a log cannot fill a locked field.

- New `dora analyse` (or corpus walk beyond the Review window)
- Content table as a grain
- Required span tree / invented parents
- ATIF emit or ingest; atifact dependency
- Pi adapter; Hub / `format:agent-traces`

- Langfuse scores / user thumbs
- Token-pressure as Skill Findings or Scan rows

### 3. Draft vertical slices

<vertical-slice-rules>

1→# Session Event IR + Session health

Published: https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/51

Grill settled 2026-08-24. ADR 0007. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Session, Event, Capture-wide, Fill when present, Parent optional, Skill invoke record, Session health, Review window). Notes: `docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md`, `docs/research-notes/49-agent-trace-approaches.md`.

Seams (please confirm): **one Session load** (adapters emit Events; load derives Session summary, Skill invoke records, and Session health) + **existing spawn-CLI** (Review Session health block, unused, `dora sessions`). No third planner. No new verb.

## Problem Statement
10→
A Reader and a Runner use Review and unused to improve context. Those commands see only a thin Session blob: tools, some text, a skill-name list. They cannot see tool errors, per-turn tokens, or cache-read share. Later we want Doraval to analyse Sessions and find gaps. The current blob cannot unlock that. `agent-traces` and Entire show what to keep (Events, tool pairs, derived skill records, token-pressure). We must not port Python, Polars, a debugger, or ATIF files this pass.

## Solution

Adapters parse each log into a list of **Events**. A **Session** summary and **Skill invoke records** are derived. Unused and Review read those records. Review adds a **Session health** block for token pressure (cache-read, call count, turn count) using Entire’s numbers. Session health is not a Finding.

The Review window stays last 10 Sessions and 30 days. Same verbs. No `dora analyse`. Fields that the log lacks stay unset. `parentId` is stored only when present. A tool is `tool_call` plus `tool_result`. ATIF is a later map, not an emit or ingest.

## User Stories

---
name: to-tickets
description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.
