1→# ADR Format

ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily — only when the first ADR is needed.

## Template

```md
10→# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}
```

That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why* — not in filling out sections.

## Optional sections

Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.
20→
- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`) — useful when decisions are revisited
- **Considered Options** — only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering
- **Consequences** — only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out

## Numbering

Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.

## When to offer an ADR
30→
All three of these must be true:

1. **Hard to reverse** — the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context** — a future reader will look at the code and wonder "why on earth did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off** — there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If a decision is easy to reverse, skip it — you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond "we did the obvious thing."

### What qualifies
40→
- **Architectural shape.** "We're using a monorepo." "The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres."
- **Integration patterns between contexts.** "Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP."
- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library — just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.
- **Boundary and scope decisions.** "Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only." The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.
- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** "We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X." Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from "fixing" something that was deliberate.
- **Constraints not visible in the code.** "We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements." "Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract."
- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it — otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.

1→# Session Event IR + Session health

Published: https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/51

Grill settled 2026-08-24. ADR 0007. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Session, Event, Capture-wide, Fill when present, Parent optional, Skill invoke record, Session health, Review window). Notes: `docs/research-notes/48-agent-traces.md`, `docs/research-notes/49-agent-trace-approaches.md`.

Seams (please confirm): **one Session load** (adapters emit Events; load derives Session summary, Skill invoke records, and Session health) + **existing spawn-CLI** (Review Session health block, unused, `dora sessions`). No third planner. No new verb.

## Problem Statement
10→
A Reader and a Runner use Review and unused to improve context. Those commands see only a thin Session blob: tools, some text, a skill-name list. They cannot see tool errors, per-turn tokens, or cache-read share. Later we want Doraval to analyse Sessions and find gaps. The current blob cannot unlock that. `agent-traces` and Entire show what to keep (Events, tool pairs, derived skill records, token-pressure). We must not port Python, Polars, a debugger, or ATIF files this pass.

## Solution

Adapters parse each log into a list of **Events**. A **Session** summary and **Skill invoke records** are derived. Unused and Review read those records. Review adds a **Session health** block for token pressure (cache-read, call count, turn count) using Entire’s numbers. Session health is not a Finding.

The Review window stays last 10 Sessions and 30 days. Same verbs. No `dora analyse`. Fields that the log lacks stay unset. `parentId` is stored only when present. A tool is `tool_call` plus `tool_result`. ATIF is a later map, not an emit or ingest.

## User Stories
20→
1. As a Runner, I want adapters to parse a Session into Events, so that later jobs have a real IR.
2. As a Runner, I want a derived Session summary (counts, token totals, duration, skills), so that Review and unused do not scan raw lines for identity.
3. As a Runner, I want unused to read Skill invoke records, so that Never invoked stays correct after the blob is gone.
4. As a Reader, I want Review to show a Session health block, so that I see token pressure next to Skill Findings.
5. As a Runner, I want Session health in Review JSON, so that I can branch without parsing a table.
6. As a Reader, I want Session health to be clearly not a Finding, so that I do not treat cache-read as a Skill defect.
7. As a Runner, I want unused to stay a Skill Finding (R034 / Never invoked), so that Session health does not replace remove logic.
8. As a Reader, I want cache-read ≥ 80% of known tokens to appear on Session health, so that I see Entire’s replay hotspot.
9. As a Reader, I want call count ≥ 20 to appear on Session health, so that I see Entire’s amplification signal.
30→10. As a Reader, I want user turns ≥ 10 to appear on Session health, so that I see a long Session.
11. As a Reader, I want no window-% or checkpoint signal, so that we do not invent Entire fields we cannot fill.
12. As a Reader, I want a Cursor Session with no tokens to omit the cache-read line, so that Fill when present holds.
13. As a Reader, I want a Session under all three thresholds to show a quiet Session health (no pressure), so that clean Sessions stay quiet.
14. As a Runner, I want Review window unchanged (10 / 30 days), so that unused does not flip on old logs.
15. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions` to still list the window, so that the list verb does not become a corpus walk.
16. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` to print tokens when known, so that “unavailable” is not a lie for Claude / Grok / Codex.
17. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` to still say tokens unavailable when unset, so that we do not invent zeros.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions show` not to dump every Event, so that Capture-wide does not become Review spam.
19. As a Runner, I want Claude `parentUuid` / tool ids stored as `parentId` / `id`, so that Later analyse can build a tree view.
40→20. As a Runner, I want Grok / Cursor / Copilot Events with unset `parentId`, so that we do not invent a span tree.
21. As a Runner, I want Claude `tool_use` and `tool_result` as two Events joined by `toolCallId`, so that `isError` has a home.
22. As a Runner, I want a tool_result with `is_error` to set `isError` on that Event, so that error rate is possible later.
23. As a Runner, I want usage tokens on the Event when Claude writes `message.usage`, so that cache-read share is real.
24. As a Runner, I want Grok / Codex list-level token totals on the Session summary when Events have none, so that we do not drop a total we already list.
25. As a Runner, I want cost on the Session summary only from Claude `result` (or equivalent), so that we do not invent dollars.
26. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for Claude Skill tool, so that unused still sees native invoke.
27. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for a slash command, so that Entire’s `prompt_slash_command` signal still counts.
28. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record for Grok titles / SKILL.md paths, so that we do not drop a proven Grok signal.
29. As a Runner, I want Cursor / Codex / Copilot Skill invoke lists to stay empty unless a proven signal appears, so that we do not guess.
50→30. As a Runner, I want no Pi adapter, so that we do not add a format with no local Doraval home.
31. As a Runner, I want a Skill invoke record to name the signal and point at source Event id(s), so that we match Entire’s derived record.
32. As a Runner, I want no synthetic `type=skill` Event, so that the Event list stays a log projection.
33. As a Runner, I want path-in-tool-input matching to remain a fallback for unused if no Skill invoke record exists, so that we do not regress today’s path evidence.
34. As a Runner, I want Plugin-owned Skills to stay skipped by unused / remove, so that the Plugin-health pass does not regress.
35. As a Runner, I want session-eval to keep working, so that adherence judge still gets tool and user text.
36. As a Runner, I want `dora review --quick` to still run without a judge, so that Session health does not require an LLM.
37. As a Runner, I want Scan to stay Skill health (no Session health block), so that Scan does not grow a second product.
38. As a Runner, I want no ATIF file written, so that we do not own schema drift this pass.
39. As a Runner, I want no ATIF ingest, so that we do not add a sixth source.
60→40. As a Runner, I want no Polars, Parquet, Hub, or Python sidecar, so that the stack stays Bun.
41. As a Runner, I want no new `dora analyse` / `dora plugin` verb, so that agent-help stays the same map plus Session health on Review.
42. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help review` to mention Session health as read-only Review output, so that the live map is not stale.
43. As a Reader, I want Review table to keep Skill Findings as they are, so that Session health is extra, not a rewrite of the Skill table.
44. As a Runner, I want Review JSON to add a `sessionHealth` object (not a Finding array row), so that clients do not treat it as R0xx.
45. As a Runner, I want `sessionHealth` to list which Sessions were considered (count, window), so that empty window is explicit.
46. As a Reader, I want zero Sessions in the window to say so on Session health, so that I do not read silence as “healthy.”
47. As a Runner, I want files over the existing size cap skipped, so that we do not change the 50 MB rule.
48. As an implementer, I want SessionPrimitives to become a derived view or to go away, so that parse is not two IRs.
49. As an implementer, I want one load function to be the only place that walks adapters, so that Review, unused, and sessions do not fork windows.
70→50. As an implementer, I want Event field unset (not 0) when missing, so that tests can tell “no tokens” from “zero tokens.”
51. As a Runner, I want `--json` and `--ci` on Review to include Session health without prompts, so that CI does not hang.
52. As a founder, I want Later analyse, Hub, scores, SDK wrap, and a web debugger out of this pass, so that we ship the IR and evidence only.

## Implementation Decisions

- Session IR is a list of Events plus a derived Session summary (ADR 0007).
- `SessionAdapter.parse` returns that Session (Events + summary). Callers do not read JSONL.
- Load still uses Review window constants (10, 30 days, 50 MB).
- Event fields (conceptual shape): `sessionId`, `seq`, `type` (`user` | `assistant` | `tool_call` | `tool_result` | `system` | `error`), optional `timestamp`, `id`, `parentId`, `toolName`, `toolCallId`, `input`, `output`, `isError`, `model`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `stopReason`.
80→- Missing log data → field omitted. Do not write 0, false, or a fake parent.

A Reader and a Runner use Review and unused to improve context. Those commands see only a thin Session blob: tools, some text, a skill-name list. 1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

20→When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

30→Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

40→- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

# CLI structure: first command, nouns, one help door

Grill settled 2026-08-24. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` § CLI-structure pass. ADRs 0008, 0009 (0004 superseded). Note: `docs/research-notes/50-cli-command-structure.md`.

**Seam (please confirm):** one **spawn-CLI** seam (existing `runDoraval` / help tests). Assert argv, exit codes, `--help` text, `--help --json` shape, and Next lines. No new planner. No second test harness.

## Problem Statement

A Reader or Runner who types `dora` gets Scan. Every Start-here line says the first job is `dora review --quick`. `--help` says both. `agent-help` is a second catalog. Nouns mix singular and plural. `new` is a grab-bag. `providers` looks like “set my Judge key” but dumps packaging specs. `bump` is a top-level maintainer verb. Flags do not mean the same thing on every command. Old names have no clean break.

## Solution

Empty `dora` prints a **short** `--help` (ADR 0008). First command stays `dora review --quick`. Scan is `dora scan` only.

Delete `agent-help`. The machine map is `dora --help --json` (ADR 0009). Text `--help` is Start here plus one-line verbs.

Create lives on the noun: `dora skill new`, `dora rule new`, `dora agent new`, `dora plugin new`. Groups are **singular** and **list** when bare. `dora skill unused` stays the Remove-candidate filter.

`reconcile` becomes `conflicts`. `sessions` becomes `session`. `rules` becomes `rule`. `bump` becomes `dora plugin bump`. Delete `providers`. Keep `dora config` (Judge keys stay `eval.*`).

Old names **hard-break**: exit `2` and one Next line. No aliases.

Flags follow dialect + escape test: `--json` and `--cwd` on every product command; writes use `--yes` / `--dry-run`; every prompt has an escape; dead Review `--for` / `--agent` go.

Same release updates README, site `/commands`, and the shipped skill (docs lockstep).

## User Stories

1. As a Runner, I want empty `dora` to print short `--help`, so that I am not launched into Scan.
2. As a Reader, I want empty `dora` to print the same Start-here as the README (`dora review --quick`), so that the first job is one line.
3. As a Runner, I want `dora scan` to still run Scan, so that the map is not gone.
4. As a Reader, I want empty `dora` not to run Review, so that I am not asked about artifact count.
5. As a Runner, I want `--help` to list verbs in one line each, so that I can pick the next command.
6. As a Runner, I want `--help` not to dump examples or exit tables, so that the first page stays short.
7. As a Runner, I want `dora --help --json` to be the live command map, so that I can parse verbs, labels, flags, and examples.
8. As a Runner, I want each map entry labeled `read-only` or `writes`, so that I know the write gate.
9. As a Runner, I want `dora review --help` to keep examples and exit codes, so that detail lives on the verb.
10. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help` to exit `2` with Next `dora --help` or `dora --help --json`, so that the second door is gone.
11. As a Runner, I want no `--capabilities` and no `agent-help` on the map, so that there is one door.
12. As a Runner, I want `dora skill` to list every Authored and Global Skill (name, origin, unused mark), so that I see the resource.
13. As a Runner, I want `dora skill unused` to stay the Remove-candidate filter, so that bare list is not unused-only.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora skill new` to scaffold a Skill, so that create sits on the noun.
15. As a Runner, I want `dora rule new` to scaffold a Rule, so that create matches the group.
16. As a Runner, I want `dora agent` to list Subagents, so that `agent` is not “which coding agent.”
17. As a Runner, I want `dora agent new` to scaffold a Subagent, so that `dora new agent` is gone.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora plugin` to list Plugins in the repo, so that Plugin is a noun.
19. As a Runner, I want `dora plugin new` to scaffold a Plugin, so that create matches the group.
20. As a Runner, I want Plugin Review to stay `dora review <plugin-root>`, so that we do not add `dora plugin review`.
21. As a Reader, I want `dora plugin bump` to raise plugin and marketplace semver, so that authors still have the version job.
22. As a Runner, I want `dora new` to exit `2` with Next pointing at `dora skill new` (or rule / agent / plugin), so that the grab-bag is gone.
23. As a Runner, I want `dora session` to list Sessions, so that the noun is singular.
24. As a Runner, I want `dora session show` to still show a Session, so that show does not move.
25. As a Runner, I want `dora sessions` to exit `2` with Next `dora session`, so that the plural is a hard break.
26. As a Runner, I want `dora rule` to list rules, so that `rules` is gone.
27. As a Runner, I want `dora rules` to exit `2` with Next `dora rule`, so that the plural is a hard break.
28. As a Runner, I want `dora memory` to list principles, so that the group lists like the others.
29. As a Runner, I want `dora config` to list keys (secrets redacted), so that the group lists and does not open a hub.
30. As a Reader, I want `dora config get` / `set` / `setup` unchanged in job, so that Judge keys stay in Config.
31. As a Reader, I want no `dora providers` and no `dora judge` verb, so that we do not add a second key command.
32. As a Runner, I want `dora providers` to exit `2` with Next `dora config setup` (keys) or `dora scan` (which agents this repo uses), so that the lying name is gone.
33. As a Runner, I want `dora bump` to exit `2` with Next `dora plugin bump`, so that bump is on the noun.
34. As a Reader, I want `dora conflicts --dry-run` to list contradictions, so that the job has a clear name.
35. As a Reader, I want `dora conflicts --yes` to apply recommended resolutions, so that `--apply` is gone.
36. As a Runner, I want `dora reconcile` to exit `2` with Next `dora conflicts`, so that the old jargon is a hard break.
37. As a Runner, I want `dora update` to stay, so that self-upgrade is not lost.
38. As a Runner, I want `--json` on every product command, so that the dialect is one machine flag.
39. As a Runner, I want `--cwd` on every product command that reads a repo, so that the isolator is one flag.
40. As a Runner, I want `--ci` to still imply JSON, so that CI scripts do not break.
41. As a Runner, I want `--format json` to still work as the old spelling, so that existing scripts keep running.
42. As a Runner, I want writes to accept `--yes` or `--dry-run` only, so that I do not guess `--apply`.
43. As a Runner, I want a write without those flags to exit `2` with Next, so that the write gate holds on `conflicts` and `plugin bump`.
44. As a Runner, I want every TTY prompt to have `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--json`, or an id, so that I never stall in a picker.
45. As a Runner, I want `review --for` and `review --agent` gone, so that planned flags cannot lie.
46. As a Runner, I want `skill --for` to still select a coding agent, so that Remove / new keep a real filter.
47. As a Reader, I want `dora --help` to name `review` before `scan` in the verb list, so that COMMANDS match Start here.
48. As a Runner, I want `dora --help --json` to list `review` before `scan`, so that the map matches the first job.
49. As a Runner, I want unknown new names (`dora nosuch`) to stay exit `1` + Next `--help`, so that hard-break `2` is only for retired verbs.
50. As a Reader, I want README Quick start and `/commands` to use the new names in the same release, so that docs lockstep holds.
51. As a Runner, I want the shipped skill to use `dora skill new`, `dora conflicts`, `dora --help --json`, and never `agent-help` / `dora new` / bare Scan, so that a cold Runner finishes the first loop.
52. As a founder, I want no 70-verb catalog, no `skills get`, no `doctor`, no MCP, and no `--help` novel, so that we stay small.
53. As a founder, I want this pass not to split Review into extra verbs, so that Review stays one gate.

## Implementation Decisions

- Respect ADR 0001 (help talks to Runner), 0002 (interactive gate), 0003 (write gate), 0008 (empty argv), 0009 (JSON map).
- Single command tree remains the source of truth for verbs and groups. Completions follow that tree.
- Empty argv invokes help, not Scan. Root flags `--json` / `--ci` / `--cwd` on empty argv still print help (JSON if asked).
- `defineGroup` bare-run becomes list, not `showUsage`, for skill / memory / rule / config / agent / plugin. `session` already lists.
- Create handlers move under those groups. Top-level `new` is removed and hard-breaks.
- Live JSON map is the existing capabilities manifest, served from `--help --json` (and `--json` on empty argv). Schema stays version + commands[] + intelligence. Drill-in `agent-help review` is not replaced; per-command `--help --json` is enough if cheap, else omit drill-in this pass.
- Hard-break table (exit `2`, one Next): `new` → `skill new` (mention rule / agent / plugin); `reconcile` → `conflicts`; `agent-help` → `--help` / `--help --json`; `rules` → `rule`; `sessions` → `session`; `bump` → `plugin bump`; `providers` → `config setup` and `scan`.
- `conflicts` keeps reconcile behavior. Drop `--apply`. `--yes` applies recommended. `--dry-run` lists.
- `plugin bump` is the old bump job (plugin.json and marketplace.json).
- Dialect: add `--json` / `--cwd` where missing on product verbs. Keep `--format` and `--ci`. Remove Review `--for` / `--agent`.
- Escape test is a checklist on every remaining TTY prompt (Scan proceed, Review artifact cap, fix, conflicts, config setup, plugin bump). Each must have a flag or id path.
- Docs lockstep in the same release: README, site get-started + `/commands`, shipped skill + command reference. CHANGELOG is not enough.
- Do not add npm deps.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external CLI behavior only. Spawn the binary. Do not assert citty internals.
- Prior art: existing CLI spawn suite (help text, `new` scaffolds, unknown command, `--json`).
- Must cover: empty argv is help (not Scan); `dora scan` still Scans; `--help` is short and names `review --quick`; `--help --json` has review-first map and no `agent-help`; each hard-break old name exits `2` with Next; `skill` / `session` / `rule` lists; `skill new` / `rule new` still write files; `conflicts --dry-run` still plans; `plugin bump --help` exists; `review --help` has no `--for` / `--agent`; `dora nosuch` stays exit `1`.
- Do not require a live Judge or network.

## Out of Scope

- New product jobs (analyse, doctor, MCP, skills get, plugin review).
- Renaming `scan` / `review` / `fix` / `new` (the word) / `config`.
- Aliases or deprecation windows.
- Dropping `--format` or `--ci`.
- Ahmad-style TTY chrome (boxen, emoji banners).
- Closing leftover parent issues #26, #32, #33, #38, #48 unless they become false.

## Further Notes

Sindre pass check: keep the surface small; tickets should be able to ship in order if needed. `conflicts` stays plural (locked). `dora agent` lists Subagents — one-line blurb on `--help`. `plugin bump` help must say it also touches marketplaces.

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

<local-ticket-template>

# <NN> — <Ticket title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

</local-ticket-template>

<issue-template>

## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

## What to build

The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Blocked by

- A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

</issue-template>

In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

</skill>
</skill_information>

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

20→When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

30→Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

40→- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

10→When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

20→A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

When the shape of that interface is itself in question — how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose — use the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

30→- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

**Empty argv:** Bare `dora` prints `--help`. It does not run Scan or Review. Scan is `dora scan` only. Same shape as agent-browser (empty argv is help, not `open`) and Entire-in-a-repo. Not Entire’s unset-repo setup flow — Doraval has no `enable`. _Avoid_: treating bare `dora` as the product job.

**This pass** is lockstep, not a docs rewrite. The binary (`dora --help`, per-command `--help`, unknown-command, `dora agent-help`) is the work. README and `/commands` change only when a new help line would disagree with them.

**agent-help:** Legacy verb. This pass **deletes** it. One text door: `dora --help` and `<cmd> --help`. Text `--help` is short: Start here + one-line verb list. Catalog and flags live on `<cmd> --help` and on `dora --help --json` (same tree, `read-only` / `writes`). `_Avoid_`: a second catalog (`agent-help`, `--capabilities`); a 400-line `--help`. See ADR 0004 (to be superseded).

**Help/agent-help pass (2026-08-20) is done when:** `dora --help` names the same first Review as the README (`dora review --quick`); `dora agent-help` exists and `--capabilities` is gone; per-command `--help` for review / fix / scan shows examples; `dora nosuch` prints one error and `Next: dora --help` (no help dump); `--json` works; agent scan skips the proceed gate; agent writes without `--yes`/`--dry-run` exit `2`; **and** README / `/commands` still agree with those lines.

| **Pass test** | This pass is done when both are true: (1) a cold Runner with only the shipped skill finishes the first loop and does not ask the human a question; (2) every verb that Runner needs is on `dora agent-help --json`, with a stable JSON shape and a Next line. |

| **Subagent this pass** | Discover only. `dora new agent` and `dora agent-help` stay (that pass). Review does not grade Subagent files. This CLI-structure pass moves create to `dora agent new` and deletes `agent-help`. |
| **Skill on agent-help** | `dora skill unused` is **read-only**. `dora skill remove` and `restore` are **writes**. Do not label the whole group as writes only. |
| **Runner verbs (this pass)** | `agent-help`, `review`, `fix`, `scan`, `sessions`, `skill unused`, `new`. `skill remove` / `restore` stay on the map as writes the human owns. |

| **This pass** | Empty argv prints `--help`. Delete `agent-help`. JSON map is `dora --help --json`. Text `--help` is a **short first page**. Help polish. `reconcile` becomes **Conflicts**. Delete `providers` (the spec dump). Keep version bump as `dora plugin bump`. Delete top-level `new`. The word stays `new` on the noun (`dora skill new`). Nouns are **singular**. Bare noun groups **list**. **Grow** = tidy existing verbs and flags. Old names are a **hard break** (exit `2` + Next). No aliases. Keep `dora config`. |

FileContent.content:
1→# doraval

Context-effectiveness CLI for coding agents. It reviews skills, rules, and memory so Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Grok work from context you can trust.

`dora` and `doraval` are the same binary. Pronunciation: *dor-uh-val* (Doraemon + eval).

## Installation

```sh
10→npm install -g @hacksmith/doraval
```

```sh
# macOS
brew tap saif-shines/tap && brew trust saif-shines/tap && brew install doraval

# Bun
bun add -g @hacksmith/doraval
```
20→
Node ≥ 14.18. Alpine/musl: use Bun. See the [installation guide](https://doraval.dev/get-started/installation/).

## Quick start

```sh
npx skills add saif-shines/doraval
dora review --quick
```

30→`--quick` is structure and heuristics only. No Judge. No API key.

You get a Review with Findings. Exit `0` clean · `1` issues · `2` could not run.

## Commands

```sh
dora                         # scan
dora review --quick .        # Findings first, no LLM
dora review --quick --json
40→dora fix . --yes             # mechanical; no TTY
dora new skill --for claude --name review-pr --yes
dora skill unused            # list Remove candidates
dora skill remove ghost --yes
dora skill restore ghost --yes
dora memory add "Never use default exports" --weight 8
dora reconcile --dry-run
dora sessions
dora sessions show <id>      # short table id is enough if unique
dora config setup
50→dora --help                  # first loop
dora agent-help              # live map
```

More: [doraval.dev/commands](https://doraval.dev/commands/).

## Building from source

Requirements:

60→- **[Bun](https://bun.sh)** ≥ 1.3
- Node ≥ 14.18 for the published binary target

```sh
bun install
bun run dev -- --help          # run CLI from source
bun run build                  # emit bin/doraval.js
```

## Repository layout
70→
| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `src/cli/` | citty CLI surface (`dora` / `doraval`) |
| `src/core/` | Scan, review, fix, memory, sessions, scaffold |
| `src/providers/` | Packaging / provider specs (`dora new`, `dora providers`) |
| `skills/doraval/` | Agent skill shipped via `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` |
| `apps/website/` | Docs site ([Blume](https://github.com/saif-shines/blume)) |
| `scripts/` | Release, platform packages, publish helpers |
| `test/` | Fixtures and CLI tests |
80→| `bin/` | Built CLI entry (`doraval.cjs`) |

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun run dev -- --help          # run from source
bun test                       # unit + CLI tests
bun run typecheck
bun run build                  # emit bin/doraval.js
90→```

FileContent.content:
1→---
name: doraval
description: "Verify agent-context quality with the `dora` CLI. Whenever you author or edit a skill (SKILL.md), plugin, rule, or agent config, run dora to check it before reporting the work done. Also use when the user asks to check, diagnose, fix, or clean up agent context across Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, or Grok. Not for ordinary source-code edits."
---

# doraval

You run `dora`. It is the verification gate on agent context: Skills, Rules, plugins, and Memory files.

10→Treat the exit code as truth. Do not report done while the code is `1` or `2`.

If `dora` is not on `PATH`, run `npx @hacksmith/doraval` in its place.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | clean | Only then report done |
| `1` | issues found | Fix or surface to the user. Do not report done |
20→| `2` | could not run | Report the failure and why. Do not claim a pass |

`--deep` Review exits `2` when no Judge is available. That is "could not run the tier you required," not clean.

## First Review

Surface Findings before JSON, LLM, or CI flags:

```bash
dora review --quick
30→```

`--quick` is structure + heuristics. No Judge. No LLM wait.

After you edit one artifact, pass its path:

```bash
dora review --quick <path>
```

40→`<path>` is the Skill directory (the folder that holds `SKILL.md`), a plugin root, or `.` for the workspace.

If Review finds more than 10 artifacts, it may ask how many to grade. Pass a path or `--all` so it does not prompt.

## Then JSON

Add `--format json` when you will branch on fields, not on a table:

```bash
dora review --quick --format json
50→```

In CI or a non-interactive subagent, add `--ci` (implies `--format json`).

Require the Judge only after a `--quick` pass is clean:

```bash
dora review --deep <path>
```

60→`--deep` exits `2` if no Judge is available. JSON keys and how to branch: [`references/output.md`](references/output.md).

## The loop

The gate is Review. Do not skip it.

1. **Review.** Run `dora review --quick` (or `dora review --quick <path>` after an edit). Read Findings. Read the exit code. Do not report done on `1` or `2`.
2. **Author** the Skill, Rule, or plugin if the user asked you to write one.
3. **Fix mechanical issues.** Preview, then apply without a TTY prompt:

70→   ```bash
   dora fix <path> --dry-run
   dora fix <path> --yes
   ```

   `--yes` applies only mechanical fixes (frontmatter, formatting, missing fields). Never run bare `dora fix`. A detected agent exits `2`. A human TTY is asked.
4. **Judgement fixes.** Anything `--yes` cannot apply comes from `dora fix <path> --brief`. Hand-edit those. Do not wait for `--yes` to do judgement work.
5. **Re-verify.** After every fix or hand-edit, run `dora review --quick <path>` again. The gate is passed only when the exit code is `0`.
6. **Delegated Judge.** If a later Review (without `--quick`) shows LLM as `via delegated` (JSON `method: "delegated"`), dora handed you the rubric. Read the `JUDGE THIS` prompt. Evaluate the Skill against it. Fix findings before you report done. Done means mechanical tiers are clean and delegated judgment is complete.
7. **Memory — only with user intent.** When the user states a durable rule to enforce:
80→
   ```bash
   dora memory add "<rule>" --weight <1-10>
   ```

   Weight is priority (1–10, default 5). `≥ 7` is a hard rule (enforced in Review). Do not invent memories from your own inferences.

   To write hard rules into `AGENTS.md`, run `dora memory promote --dry-run`, then `dora memory promote --yes` only when the user wants that. Never run bare `promote`. It prompts.
8. **Contradictions.** If Review or Scan reports a cross-agent conflict, run `dora reconcile --dry-run` and ask the user. Never run bare `reconcile`. Use `--apply` only after the user confirms.

90→## When to reach for each verb

| Moment | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Entering a repo with agent context you did not write | `dora review --quick` |
| Just wrote or edited a Skill, Rule, or plugin | `dora review --quick <path>` |
| Branch on fields | add `--format json` |
| CI / non-interactive subagent | add `--ci` |
| Mechanical errors in Findings | `dora fix <path> --dry-run`, then `--yes` |
| User states a durable rule | `dora memory add "<rule>" --weight <1-10>` |
100→| Two agents disagree | `dora reconcile --dry-run`, then ask the user |
| Fast workspace check (no Review) | `dora --yes` (bare Scan; `--yes` skips the TTY confirm) |
| Find unused Authored Skills | `dora skill unused` |
| Scan or Review reports R034 Remove candidate | `dora skill unused`, then `dora skill remove <name> --dry-run`, then `--yes` |
| Need a Quarantined Global Skill back | `dora skill restore <name> --yes` |

## Constraints

You run in a loop that cannot answer TTY prompts.

110→- MUST treat the exit code as truth: `0` clean, `1` issues, `2` could not run. MUST NOT report done on `1` or `2`.
- MUST run `dora review --quick` first so Findings show before `--format json`.
- MUST apply `fix`, `memory promote`, `skill remove`, and `skill restore` with `--yes` or `--dry-run`. MUST NOT run bare `dora fix`, `dora reconcile`, `dora memory promote`, `dora skill remove`, or `dora skill restore`.
- MUST NOT write to `dora memory` from your own inference. Add a memory only when the user states a durable rule.
- MUST add `--ci` in CI or a non-interactive subagent.
- MUST look up flags with `dora <command> --help`. MUST NOT copy a flag catalog into this skill.

Bare Scan (`dora`) asks a human on a TTY. A detected agent skips that gate. Use `dora --yes` or `dora --json` if you want no prompt. Live command map: `dora agent-help` (add `--json` to parse). Short verb list: [`references/commands.md`](references/commands.md).

## What dora does not do
120→
dora does not write the Skill for you. It does not invent a pass. It diagnoses, applies mechanical fixes (`--yes`), and records user-stated decisions. Judgement fixes come back as a brief (`dora fix --brief`).

1→---
title: Commands
description: Pasteable dora commands. Flags live on --help.
sidebar:
  label: Commands
  order: 1
---

`dora` and `doraval` are the same binary. Use `npx @hacksmith/doraval` if `dora` is not on `PATH`.
10→
```bash
dora --help                  # first loop + command list
dora review --help           # this command
dora agent-help              # live map (add --json to parse)
```

Exit `0` clean · `1` issues · `2` could not run.

## Scan
20→
```bash
dora                         # workspace health (alias: dora scan)
dora --json                  # same as --format json
dora --ci                    # implies JSON
dora --cwd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
```

Read-only. No LLM. No API key.

30→## Review

```bash
dora review --quick .        # structure + heuristics; Findings first
dora review --quick ./path/to/skill-dir
dora review --all --quick --ci
dora review --deep .         # require Judge; exit 2 if none
dora review --sessions .     # require session evidence
dora review CLAUDE.md
dora review --json           # includes sessionHealth (not --quick)
40→```

`--quick` is the first Review. It does not include Session health. A full Review adds a Session health block (token pressure). That block is not a Finding.

JSON comes after:

```bash
dora review --quick --json
```

50→Tiers: [Review tiers](/concepts/review-tiers/).

## Fix

```bash
dora fix . --dry-run
dora fix . --yes             # mechanical; no TTY
dora fix . --brief           # judgment items, then edit
```

60→Re-run `dora review --quick` until exit `0`.

## New

```bash
dora new skill --for claude --name review-pr --description "Reviews PRs" --yes
dora new rule --for cursor --name no-default-exports --yes
dora new plugin --for claude --name my-plugin --yes
```

70→Always pass `--for`. Then `dora review --quick` the new path.

## Skill

```bash
dora skill unused
dora skill remove ghost --dry-run
dora skill remove ghost --yes
dora skill remove ghost --for claude --yes
dora skill restore ghost --yes
80→```

`dora skill unused` lists Remove candidates. It writes nothing.

Deletes an Authored Skill. Quarantines a Global Skill (home copy). Restore puts that copy back.

A detected agent needs `--yes` or `--dry-run`. A name clash needs `--for`, `--global`, or a path.

Scan and Review mark an Authored Skill that was never invoked in the Review window, and is not a Recent install, as [R034](/reference/rules/R034). That is a Remove candidate. A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from one project’s Sessions.

90→## Memory

```bash
dora memory add "Never use default exports" --weight 8
dora memory add "Prefer named exports" --global
dora memory list
dora memory promote          # hard rules → AGENTS.md
dora memory promote --dry-run
dora memory context --json --quiet
dora memory stash path/to/notes.md
100→dora memory restore path/to/notes.md
dora memory sync
```

Weights: **8+** hard · **5** default · **1–3** soft. [Memory](/concepts/memory/).

## Reconcile

```bash
dora reconcile --dry-run
110→dora reconcile --apply --yes
```

Settles Claude-vs-Cursor contradictions into `AGENTS.md`.

## Sessions

```bash
dora sessions
dora sessions --agent claude --limit 20
120→dora sessions show <sessionId>
dora sessions --json
```

Read-only. Adapters: Claude, Grok, Cursor, Codex, Copilot.

The table shortens the id. `show` accepts that short id when it is unique. `--json` has the full `sessionId`. `show` prints token totals when the log has them. It says `unavailable` when it does not.

## Config

130→```bash
dora config                  # TTY hub
dora config setup            # Judge wizard
dora config get eval.model
dora config set eval.model gpt-4.1
dora config set eval.judge auto
```

`--deep` needs a Judge. Do not paste API keys into chat.

140→## Bump

```bash
dora bump patch
dora bump minor ./plugins
dora bump 1.2.3 --yes
```

## Providers

150→```bash
dora providers               # packaging matrix, not “who is installed”
dora providers --json
```

Who is installed is `dora` (scan).

## Update

```bash
160→dora update
dora update --check
dora update --via npm
```

## Agent-help

```bash
dora agent-help              # every verb, read-only vs writes
dora agent-help --json       # same tree
170→dora agent-help review       # one verb
```

Replaces `--capabilities`.

## Completions

```bash
dora --completion bash
dora --completion zsh
180→dora --completion fish

1→# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 0.6.26

### Docs

- Feature release requires docs lockstep (`AGENTS.md`): website, README, and
10→  the shipped skill must match the binary before tag.

## 0.6.25

### Features

- Session parse is an **Event list** plus a derived summary. Tool call and
  result are paired. Tokens, errors, and `parentId` are set only when the
  log has them.
- Unused and Review read **Skill invoke records** (Claude Skill tool, slash
20→  command, Grok titles).
- Review (not `--quick`) prints a **Session health** block for token
  pressure: cache-read ≥ 80%, calls ≥ 20, turns ≥ 10. Not a Finding.
- `dora sessions show` prints token totals when known. A short table id
  is enough when it is unique.

  the shipped skill must match the binary before tag.

## 0.6.25

### Features

- Session parse is an **Event list** plus a derived summary. Tool call and
  result are paired. Tokens, errors, and `parentId` are set only when the

# Writing Commit Messages

## Overview

Every commit message follows a consistent format. The subject line completes the sentence: **"If applied, this commit will _\<your subject line\>_"**. When present, the body explains **why**, not what.

## Detect Project Convention First
20→
Follow existing instructions for commits if present in the repository. Check `git log --oneline -20` to see recent patterns and match the existing style.

**Project convention always wins.** The rules below are the default when no convention is detected.

## References

Consider the following references when creating new commit messages:
- **Subject line rules, body format, URLs, issue references**: [references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md](references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md)
- **Split strategies, anti-rationalizations, and refactoring patterns**: [references/ATOMIC_COMMITS.md](references/ATOMIC_COMMITS.md)
30→- **Complete red flags checklist and mistake patterns**: [references/COMMON_MISTAKES.md](references/COMMON_MISTAKES.md)

# Docs writing style

Two modes. Choose one per session.

| Mode | When to use | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **Handoff** | Before writing — you want your coding agent (Claude/Cursor/Copilot) to match the existing voice | A self-contained prompt block to paste into your coding agent's system instructions |
20→| **Review** | After drafting — you want to check your draft's tone, structure, and style before submitting | A rubric-based diagnosis: what passes, what needs fixing, in priority order |

State your mode at the start: "handoff" or "review."

---

## Core principle

**Documentation voice is a contract with the reader.** Inconsistent tone makes docs feel untrustworthy. Consistent tone — even across many contributors — makes readers confident the information is accurate.

30→---

## Handoff mode

> Load `references/style-principles.md` for the full principles list.
> Load `references/scalekit-style-prompt-block.md` (or `<docs-repo>/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` if the consumer has one) for the site-specific prompt block.

In handoff mode:
1. Load the style prompt block for this docs site.
2. Present it directly — the contributor pastes it into their coding agent's system instructions or project-level CLAUDE.md / `.cursorrules` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
40→3. Optionally: if the contributor describes what they are writing (e.g., "a how-to guide for agent auth"), append a 2–3 line supplement tailoring the prompt to that content type.

The prompt block is self-contained. The contributor does not need to explain the docs site to their coding agent — the prompt does it for them.

---

## Review mode

> Load `references/style-principles.md` for the full principles list.
> Load `references/llms-judge-rubric.md` for the quality rubric.
50→
In review mode:
1. Ask for the draft (a file path, a pasted block, or both).
2. Run the rubric against the draft.
3. Report findings in this format:

```
PASS   <criterion> — <brief note if anything to mention>
FAIL   <criterion> — <specific problem> → fix: <what to do>
WARN   <criterion> — <borderline issue worth watching>
60→```

4. Group by priority: fails first, warns second, passes last.
5. End with one sentence: the most impactful single fix, if any.

Do not flag style issues in code blocks. Code is reviewed separately.

---

## Key rules (quick reference)
70→
These apply regardless of mode. Violations in review mode are always FAIL.

**Structure**
- Sentence case for all headings. No "Configure Your Auth Provider" — use "Configure your auth provider."
- Page opens with a clear one-paragraph statement: what the reader will do and why.
- Procedure steps use imperative verbs: "Install", "Run", "Configure" — not "Installing", "You should run."
- H2 for major sections; H3 for subsections. Never use H1 in body content.
- **Step headings inside `<Steps>` must be H3 (`###`) or smaller** — never H2. H2 inside Steps creates oversized step titles that break visual hierarchy.
- **Single-item lists are not lists.** If a section (e.g. Prerequisites) has only one bullet or numbered item, remove the list markup and write it as a plain paragraph or a smaller heading with prose.
80→
**Language**
- Active voice: "Run the command" not "The command should be run."
- Second person: "you" for instructions, not "the developer" or "users."
- Present tense: "This method returns" not "This method will return."
- No filler: no "just", "simply", "basically", "obviously", "quickly", "we're excited."
- Expand abbreviations on first use: "single sign-on (SSO)" not just "SSO."

**Code**
- All four SDK languages (Node.js, Python, Go, Java) in `<Tabs syncKey="tech-stack">` for 90% of SDK examples.
90→- SDK variable names are NON-NEGOTIABLE: `scalekit` (Node.js), `scalekit_client` (Python), `scalekitClient` (Go/Java).
- No hardcoded secrets. Environment variables only. Add a comment explaining the security reason.
- Show error paths alongside the happy path.
- Examples must be runnable or explicitly marked as pseudocode.

**Asides and callouts**
- `<Aside>` is for incidental context only — cautions, tips, notes.
- Never put required steps or critical information inside an `<Aside>`.
- Use `type="caution"`, `type="tip"`, or `type="note"` with a `title` attribute.

100→**Links**
- Descriptive link text only. Never "click here" or "this link."
- Backticks for code identifiers, file paths, environment variables, and API endpoints.

---

## Did this help?

At the end of every session, ask: **"Did this solve what you were trying to do?"**

110→- If yes: done.
- If the style prompt was wrong for your site, the review missed something, or the rubric produced unhelpful output: encourage the user to file an issue at **https://github.com/saif-shines/devex-kit/issues**. Offer to help draft it using their agent — include: which mode they used, what they were reviewing or writing, and what was wrong or missing.

---

## Adapt to your docs site

This skill is site-agnostic. The Scalekit-specific prompt block is in `references/scalekit-style-prompt-block.md`. To adapt:

1. Copy `references/_template-style-prompt-block.md` → `<your-docs-repo>/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md`.
120→2. Fill in your site's voice, SDK naming conventions, and code standards.
3. The skill checks for `<docs-repo>/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` first; falls back to the Scalekit sample with a note that it is an example.

1→# Documentation style principles

Generic principles for developer-facing technical documentation. These apply to any docs site. Site-specific conventions (SDK variable names, component usage, code standards) live in the site's style prompt block.

## Structure

- **Sentence case** for all headings: "Configure your auth provider" not "Configure Your Auth Provider."
- **Short, descriptive page titles**: 3–7 words. Headings describe outcomes, not categories.
- **Imperative headings**: "Configure proxies" not "Configuring proxies" or "Proxy configuration."
10→- **Opening paragraph**: 1–3 sentences. State what the reader will accomplish, when they need it, and the approach. No "In this guide" or "Welcome to."
- **One idea per paragraph**. Short paragraphs are easier to skim than long ones.
- **Topic sentences are standalone**: the first sentence of each section or paragraph should be understandable without reading what came before it.
- **Key takeaways at the top**: conclusion before reasoning, result before procedure.
- **Use bullets and tables** to structure lists of items, comparisons, and options. Never use prose to list things that would read better as a table.

## Language

- **Active voice**: "Run the command" not "The command should be run."
- **Second person**: "you" for instructions — not "the developer", "the user", or "one."
20→- **Present tense**: "This method returns" not "This method will return."
- **Imperative for procedures**: "Install", "Create", "Run", "Configure", "Test."
- **Front-load the action**: start sentences with the verb or key concept.
- **Short sentences**: break any sentence that requires a second read.
- **Right-branching structure**: main clause first, subordinate clause after. "Run this command before restarting" not "Before restarting, run this command."
- **Explicit noun references**: replace "this", "these", "that" with the actual noun. "This configuration" → "The timeout configuration."

## Tone

- **Direct and concise**: no hedging, no filler.
30→- **Neutral and professional**: no hype, no marketing copy, no excitement markers.
- **Assume competence**: write for a capable developer who is new to this particular tool or API.
- **Audience-first**: explain what matters to someone trying to get work done, not what is interesting to someone who built the feature.

## Forbidden patterns

| Pattern | Replace with |
|---|---|
| "Just", "simply", "easily" | Remove or rephrase |
| "Obviously", "clearly", "of course" | Remove |
40→| "We're excited to announce" | State the fact directly |
| "Click here" or "this link" | Descriptive link text |
| Passive voice in procedures | Active imperative |
| Gerund headings ("Configuring…") | Imperative ("Configure…") or noun ("Configuration") |
| Socratic build-up (context → theory → conclusion) | Conclusion first, then support |

## Code in documentation

- Use code blocks with language identifiers for all code snippets.
- Never use screenshots of code — text blocks are searchable, copyable, and maintainable.
50→- Keep examples minimal and self-contained.
- Show error paths alongside success paths.
- Never hardcode secrets or API keys. Use environment variables. Add a comment explaining why.
- Expand imports only when they are not obvious; collapse with `collapse` if they are noisy.

## Callouts and asides

- `Aside type="caution"` — warns of a consequence the reader might not expect.
- `Aside type="tip"` — offers a useful shortcut or alternative.
- `Aside type="note"` — adds context that is helpful but not required.
60→- Always include a `title` attribute on `<Aside>`.
- Never use `<Aside>` for required steps, critical warnings that block success, or primary content. Those belong in the body.

## Links

- Descriptive anchor text: "See the authentication guide" not "click here" or "see this."
- Backticks for code: variables, functions, endpoints, file paths, environment variables, and command-line flags.
- Relative links for internal pages.

## Abbreviations
70→
- Expand on first use: "single sign-on (SSO)" then "SSO" thereafter.
- Do not assume readers know your product's internal acronyms or team shorthands.

1→# Documentation style principles

Generic principles for developer-facing technical documentation. These apply to any docs site. Site-specific conventions (SDK variable names, component usage, code standards) live in the site's style prompt block.

## Structure

- **Sentence case** for all headings: "Configure your auth provider" not "Configure Your Auth Provider."
- **Short, descriptive page titles**: 3–7 words. Headings describe outcomes, not categories.
- **Imperative headings**: "Configure proxies" not "Configuring proxies" or "Proxy configuration."
10→- **Opening paragraph**: 1–3 sentences. State what the reader will accomplish, when they need it, and the approach. No "In this guide" or "Welcome to."
- **One idea per paragraph**. Short paragraphs are easier to skim than long ones.
- **Topic sentences are standalone**: the first sentence of each section or paragraph should be understandable without reading what came before it.
- **Key takeaways at the top**: conclusion before reasoning, result before procedure.
- **Use bullets and tables** to structure lists of items, comparisons, and options. Never use prose to list things that would read better as a table.

## Language

- **Active voice**: "Run the command" not "The command should be run."
- **Second person**: "you" for instructions — not "the developer", "the user", or "one."
20→- **Present tense**: "This method returns" not "This method will return."
- **Imperative for procedures**: "Install", "Create", "Run", "Configure", "Test."
- **Front-load the action**: start sentences with the verb or key concept.
- **Short sentences**: break any sentence that requires a second read.
- **Right-branching structure**: main clause first, subordinate clause after. "Run this command before restarting" not "Before restarting, run this command."
- **Explicit noun references**: replace "this", "these", "that" with the actual noun. "This configuration" → "The timeout configuration."

## Tone

- **Direct and concise**: no hedging, no filler.
30→- **Neutral and professional**: no hype, no marketing copy, no excitement markers.
- **Assume competence**: write for a capable developer who is new to this particular tool or API.
- **Audience-first**: explain what matters to someone trying to get work done, not what is interesting to someone who built the feature.

## Forbidden patterns

| Pattern | Replace with |
|---|---|
| "Just", "simply", "easily" | Remove or rephrase |
| "Obviously", "clearly", "of course" | Remove |
40→| "We're excited to announce" | State the fact directly |
| "Click here" or "this link" | Descriptive link text |
| Passive voice in procedures | Active imperative |
| Gerund headings ("Configuring…") | Imperative ("Configure…") or noun ("Configuration") |
| Socratic build-up (context → theory → conclusion) | Conclusion first, then support |

## Code in documentation

- Use code blocks with language identifiers for all code snippets.
- Never use screenshots of code — text blocks are searchable, copyable, and maintainable.
50→- Keep examples minimal and self-contained.
- Show error paths alongside success paths.
- Never hardcode secrets or API keys. Use environment variables. Add a comment explaining why.
- Expand imports only when they are not obvious; collapse with `collapse` if they are noisy.

## Callouts and asides

- `Aside type="caution"` — warns of a consequence the reader might not expect.
- `Aside type="tip"` — offers a useful shortcut or alternative.
- `Aside type="note"` — adds context that is helpful but not required.
60→- Always include a `title` attribute on `<Aside>`.
- Never use `<Aside>` for required steps, critical warnings that block success, or primary content. Those belong in the body.

## Links

- Descriptive anchor text: "See the authentication guide" not "click here" or "see this."
- Backticks for code: variables, functions, endpoints, file paths, environment variables, and command-line flags.
- Relative links for internal pages.

## Abbreviations
70→
- Expand on first use: "single sign-on (SSO)" then "SSO" thereafter.
- Do not assume readers know your product's internal acronyms or team shorthands.

1→# doraval docs style prompt block
